development_data: Literature-derived A2AR regulatory network (Biorelate NLP + Ingenuity curation), filtered for expression in human tumours (TCGA median) and presence on the NanoString PanCancer Immune panel (14 genes); biological validation in mouse syngeneic models, A2AR-KO NK cells, TCGA, and a phase IA AZD4635 trial (n=7). ICB testing only in Prat 2017 (anti-PD-1, n=65) and Chen PL 2016 (anti-CTLA-4 NanoString, n=53), neither among the 12.
evidence: Methods 'Signature generation and scoring': genes filtered as downstream of/upregulated by A2AR, 'robustly expressed in human tumors... median expression greater than the median expression of all genes', and present on the Nanostring PanCancer Immune Profiling panel (14 genes). Methods 'Analysis of public datasets': 'Published cohorts of immunotherapy-treated subjects ... were obtained from refs. (35, 36)'. Results 'Adenosine signaling is prognostic for immunotherapy response': 'Prat and colleagues generated gene expression profiles of 65 patients ... treated with anti-PD1 therapy (35). Chen and colleagues profiled 53 patients with metastatic melanoma ... anti-CTLA-4 therapy (36).' Ref 35 = Prat A 2017 Cancer Res (PMID 28487385), ref 36 = Chen PL 2016 Cancer Discov (PMID 27301722) (reference numbers mapped via Europe PMC reference list, since the full text's REFERENCES section is empty). None of the 12 cohorts (Hugo, Riaz, Van Allen, Mariathasan, etc.) is mentioned anywhere in the text. Other ICB cohorts used (not among the 12): Prat 2017 (anti-PD-1 NanoString, NSCLC/HNSCC/melanoma), Chen PL 2016 MDACC (anti-CTLA-4 NanoString), NCT02740985 AZD4635 phase IA (A2AR inhibitor +/- durvalumab; pharmacodynamics only). Sources: (https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/26/9/2176/83069/Adenosine-Signaling-Is-Prognostic-for-Cancer ; doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-19-2183); https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/MED/31953314/references | Caveats: Supplementary Fig. S7 'Adenosine signature score cut-point determination from the Prat & Chen et al cohorts' (logistic regression for response probability) used ICB outcome in those two non-12 cohorts for a cut-point; gene selection itself used no outcome. Main survival analyses split scores at 0. SignatureSets text ('reduced efficacy of anti-PD1 therapy in published cohorts') refers to Prat/Chen, not any of the 12.

development_data: 17 literature APM genes refined to 8 (B2M, CALR, NLRC5, PSMB9, PSME1, PSME3, RFX5, HSP90AB1) by keeping genes with nominal p<0.05 positive association with response in the own Penn NSCLC anti-PD-1/PD-L1 cohort (n=51, AmpliSeq; not among the 12).
evidence: Methods 'Gene signature generation': 'Genes in this expanded antigen processing signature were examined to determine differential expression between responders and non-responders. A refined antigen processing signature was then generated by removal of genes that did not reach a nominal p value of less 0.05 for a positive association with response. This resulted in an eight-gene APMS' (own Penn NSCLC cohort). Methods 'Melanoma cohorts': 'An additional publicly available melanoma data set with RNA sequencing was utilized to assess the antigen processing score and association with outcomes.34 This cohort included 27 metastatic melanoma patients treated with pembrolizumab. The refined eight-gene APM log2 z-score was assessed for its association with response'. Results 'The APMS in melanoma predicts response': 'To evaluate the generalizability of the APMS ... in an additional tumor type' (response p=0.09, AUC 0.68; OS HR 0.29). Ref 34 = Hugo W Cell 2016 (PMID 26997480). 'Kim' appears only as an author name in ref 21 (Campbell JD et al. Nat Genet 2016) and refers to no cohort; Kim 2018 gastric cohort not used. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own Penn NSCLC cohort (development/discovery, n=51), Huang AC 2019 Nat Med neoadjuvant pembrolizumab melanoma NanoString (n=14, 7-gene partial APM; validation). Sources: (PMC7542663, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7542663/) | Caveats: Hugo was used only to test the frozen 8-gene score (median split for OS). Only 27 of Hugo's patients analysed.

development_data: APM gene list (18 genes) taken from a review (Leone 2013); per-sample GSVA score (APS). TIGS = APS normalised to TCGA pan-cancer min/max x ln(TMB+1); a pan-cancer correlation with aggregate anti-PD-(L)1 ORRs from published trials (APS from TCGA/GEO, TMB from Foundation Medicine). No fitted parameters.
evidence: Results 'APM score definition': 'On the basis of a review paper about APM (Leone et al., 2013), the following genes were selected for quantification: PSMB5 ... HLA-C'. Methods 'Collection and analysis of immunotherapy genomics datasets': 'To evaluate the power of TIGS to predict clinical response to ICIs, we searched PubMed for ICI clinical studies for which TMB and gene transcriptome information was available ... three datasets ... The Van Allen et al. (2015) dataset was downloaded from the supplementary files ... The Hugo et al. (2016) dataset was downloaded from the supplementary files ...' Fig 5: ROC in 35 Van Allen anti-CTLA4 melanoma and 27 Hugo anti-PD-1 melanoma patients; 'APS itself also shows improved or similar prediction power' (Fig 5D-F); KM curves by within-dataset median. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): Snyder 2017 urothelial atezolizumab (22 pts; hammerlab GitHub); aggregate trial ORRs (Figure 4 source data). Riaz and Miao are cited only in the reference list (Chowell 2018; Miao 2018 Nat Genet), not used. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6879305/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/APM_Wang.csv | Caveats: V for Hugo and Van_Allen because APS/TIGS were fully fixed beforehand (literature genes, TCGA normalisation) and the authors frame these datasets as an evaluation. Borderline C: these three datasets (Van Allen, Hugo, Snyder) were analysed side by side and are the paper's only patient-level ICB evidence, so the claim that APS/TIGS predicts individual response arises from them jointly; there was no separate ICB discovery cohort. No tuning on them was seen. The aggregate ORR analysis used trial-level ORRs only, not cohort expression data.

development_data: Predefined 8-gene B-cell marker set from Danaher et al. 2017 (BLK, CD19, FCRL2, MS4A1, TNFRSF17, TCL1A, SPIB, PNOC; NanoString PanCancer Immune panel); tested in own Heidelberg lung adenocarcinoma ICB cohort (n=43; not among 12) and in TCGA LUAD (n=506, non-ICB prognostic comparison).
evidence: Methods 'Absolute and relative scores of immune cell infiltration': 'The abundance of 14 immune cell populations ... was estimated from the mRNA expression of marker genes as described before.19 ... The B cell expression signature included the eight marker genes BLK, CD19, FCRL2, MA4A1, TNFRSF17, TCL1A, SPIB, and PNOC' (ref 19 = Danaher 2017). Methods 'Study cohort': '43 patients diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma ... treated with ICB at the Thoraxklinik of Heidelberg University Hospital'. Results: 'B cells with HR = 0.66 (0.52-0.84, p = .00074)' (own cohort), TCGA LUAD used as non-ICB comparison. No public ICB cohort is analysed: Van Allen (ref 4), Hugo (author in ref 7, Shin 2017), Kim (author names only, refs 5 and 32) and Hwang 2020 (ref 32) appear only as citations; Jung 2019 Samsung NSCLC is not cited or used. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own Heidelberg LUAD cohort (discovery/claim). Sources: (PMC7808386, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7808386/) | Caveats: Gene content is predefined (Danaher markers, no outcome), but the B-cell score was singled out as the lead marker among 14 cell-type scores by its association with PFS/response in the own cohort (FDR<10%); that is signature-level selection on own-cohort ICB outcome, not gene selection, so outcome_guided=no. None of the 12 cohorts was used.

development_data: 66 genes = Helmink Supplementary Table 24: genes up in B cells of responders vs non-responders in scRNA-seq (Smart-seq2, CD45+CD19+ cells; 48 samples from 32 ICB-treated metastatic melanoma pts = Sade-Feldman et al. 2018 dataset, ref 44, which includes some MDACC neoadjuvant pts). Selection used Fisher's exact test, Bonferroni q<=0.05, log2FC>0.5. The paper's bulk B-cell claims (MDACC neoadjuvant melanoma NCT02519322, OpACIN-neo, MDACC RCC NCT02210117) used MCP-counter B lineage genes, not this list.
evidence: Results 'BCR and single-cell RNA-seq offer functional insight': 'Unbiased analysis for markers of B cells (using all expressed genes in the CD45+CD19+ population only) associated with clinical outcome demonstrated 46 markers were significantly enriched in lesions from responders and 147 markers ... in non-responder lesions (Extended Data Fig. 9b, Supplementary Tables 24, 25)'. Methods 'Patient cohort(s)': 'The single-cell RNA-seq B cell analysis used a dataset from 32 patients with metastatic melanoma (n = 48 samples) treated with anti-PD1 (n = 37), anti-CTLA4 (n = 2), or anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 (n = 9)44'; ref 44 = Sade-Feldman, Cell 2018. Supplementary Table 24 ('Differentially expressed genes increased in B-cells analyzed by single cell RNAseq in metastatic melanoma patients responding to immune checkpoint blockade') lists 66 genes, which match the SignatureSets list exactly after symbol updates (TMEM2=CEMIP2, FAIM3=FCMR, KIAA1683=IQCN, PRMT10=PRMT9, KIAA0226L=RUBCNL, LOH12CR1=BORCS5, FAM46C=TENT5C). None of Van Allen, Riaz, Gide, Hugo or the other 12 is mentioned anywhere in the paper. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): MDACC neoadjuvant melanoma (NCT02519322), OpACIN-neo (NCT02437279), MDACC pre-surgical RCC (NCT02210117), Sade-Feldman 2018 scRNA. Non-ICB: neoadjuvant dabrafenib/trametinib (NCT02231775), TCGA SKCM/KIRC. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8762581/ ; https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-019-1922-8/MediaObjects/41586_2019_1922_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/Bcell_Helmink.csv | Caveats: outcome_guided=yes: responder vs non-responder differential expression in an ICB scRNA cohort that is not among the 12 (Sade-Feldman is explicitly excluded). The text says 46 responder markers, but Supp Table 24 has 66 rows; SignatureSets uses all 66. Published Jan 2020.

development_data: Peripheral whole blood (PAXgene) qPCR 169-gene panel; tremelimumab phase III melanoma (treatment-naive, n=210, discovery) -> 15-gene correlated-component-regression classifier; validated in tremelimumab phase IIb (chemo-refractory, n=150)
evidence: Friedlander et al. JITC 2017 (PMC5557000; local txt 28807052.txt). Abstract/Methods: 'Peripheral blood samples ... from 210 treatment-naive melanoma patients receiving tremelimumab in a ... phase III study (discovery dataset)... A 15-gene pre-treatment response-predictive classifier model was identified. An independent population (N=150) of refractory melanoma patients receiving tremelimumab after chemotherapy ... phase II study (validation dataset)'; Statistical analysis: '2-gene core models' trained on discovery and 'At each step, resulting classifier models were validated for response and survival on the validation dataset' (so the phase IIb set also guided model building). 15 genes (ADAM17, CDK2, CDKN2A, DPP4, ERBB2, HLA-DRA, ICOS, ITGA4, LARGE, MYC, NAB2, NRAS, RHOC, TGFB1, TIMP1) = bhklab. No tumour RNA, no public cohort; ipilimumab only mentioned in background. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5557000/ | Caveats: Other ICB cohorts (not among 12): tremelimumab phase III (Ribas 2013) and phase IIb (Kirkwood 2010) blood samples. Blood-derived qPCR classifier applied to tumour RNA in the 12 cohorts is a platform/tissue shift; bhklab weights NA (CCR coefficients not used) and bhklab description ('whole-blood RNA-Sequencing', 'microarray') is inaccurate (qPCR). Only tremelimumab, not ipilimumab, was used.

development_data: TCGA pan-cancer (15 types; 8,043 tumour vs 704 normal): GO 'extracellular matrix' genes differentially expressed tumour vs normal (limma, FDR<0.01, 2FC) -> 58 C-ECM genes (30 up, 28 down)
evidence: Gene definition (Results 'Definition of a pan-cancer ECM dysregulation profile' / Methods 'Analysis of ECM signatures in cancer'): 'This identified 58 out of the 249 ECM genes ... to be cancer associated (C-ECM genes) ... comprising 30 out of the 522 upregulated genes, and 28 out of the 644 downregulated genes' (bhklab = 58 genes). TCGA survival used only to characterise (C-ECM-up prognostic, down not). C for Hugo and Riaz (Results 'C-ECM dysregulation predicts failure of PD-1 blockade'; Methods 'Analysis of immunotherapy data sets'): 'In two out of three cohorts of PD-1-blockade-treated patients (two melanoma, one bladder)37-39 [37 = Snyder 2017 urothelial atezolizumab, 38 = Hugo 2016, 39 = Riaz 2017], the C-ECM-up score was significantly higher in progressors' (Fig. 4a: SKCM_Pembrolizumab [Hugo] p=0.006 up, p=0.01 down; SKCM_Nivolumab [Riaz] ns; BLCA_Atezolizumab [Snyder] p=0.03); 'pooled logistic regression accounting for cancer type, CYT, mutational load, a T cell-inflamed signature, cohort ...' and 0.632 bootstrap model comparison on the pooled three cohorts. The three cohorts were analysed jointly/symmetrically and are the only ICB data, so the ICB claim was first established in them (no separate validation). Derived 19-gene 'practical signature': 'restricted hypothesis testing using limma-trend found 19 C-ECM genes overexpressed at FDR < 0.1 between responders and nonresponders' in pooled ICB data -> that subset would be D for Hugo/Riaz, but bhklab uses the full 58-gene set. CTLA-4 data (Van Allen) explicitly excluded: 'We did not include CTLA4-blockade data because of the small number of patients'. Mariathasan/IMvigor210 not used; BLCA cohort = Snyder 2017 (not among 12). URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6224529/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-06654-8 (Fig. 4a image) | Caveats: C rather than D because the 58 genes were fixed from TCGA tumour-vs-normal DE before ICB analysis; the logistic/bootstrap models fit on the pooled ICB cohorts are evaluation models, not part of the 58-gene ssGSEA signature. If the 19-gene ICB-derived subset were evaluated instead, Hugo and Riaz would be D. Response definition here: PR/CR/SD vs PD. | Reconciliation: per the coding rule that development on non-ICB data rules out D/C, cohorts in which a signature frozen on non-ICB data was only tested are coded V; C is kept only where analysis of the cohort itself motivated/shaped the signature. Hugo and Riaz changed from C to V: the 58-gene C-ECM set was fixed from TCGA tumour-vs-normal before ICB testing (Results "C-ECM dysregulation predicts failure of PD-1 blockade": "In two out of three cohorts of PD-1-blockade-treated patients ... refs 37-39"). BORDERLINE: these were the only ICB cohorts behind the claim (pooled with Snyder 2017), and the paper's separate 19-gene "practical signature" was selected by responder-vs-nonresponder limma in pooled Hugo+Riaz+Snyder (D if that subset were used; bhklab uses the full 58 genes). (first reading coded Hugo=C, Riaz=C)

development_data: Non-ICB public expression data: CCL5hi/CXCL9hi groups defined in curatedOvarianData (2402 serous EOC, 16 studies incl. TCGA) and in TCGA melanoma, TNBC, colon and lung collections; ~200 genes up in CCL5hiCXCL9hi tumours per tumour type, intersected into a 21-gene common signature; plus human ovarian ex vivo and mouse mechanistic work.
evidence: STAR Methods 'Bioinformatics and Statistical Analyses': 'To define the physiologically most adequate cutoffs for classifying tumors as CCL5hiCXCL9hi we investigated by visual inspection curves of estimated survival in dependence of the gene level' (non-ICB OS/RFS); 'For intersection analysis and pathway analysis we took the top 202 highly differentially expressed genes in each of the five tumor types.' Results: 'We merged these to derive a final common 21-gene signature ... shared across all five-cancer types.' ICB data used only for testing: 'Signature scores were calculated for RNA-seq transcriptome profiles of pre-treatment samples from melanoma trial Checkmate 064 (Rodig et al., 2018)' (nivolumab-then-ipilimumab arm AUC 78.7%; association lost in ipilimumab-then-nivolumab arm, Fig S5), and on-treatment NanoString data 'extracted from the Supplementary Table 6 of Chen et al. (Chen et al., 2016)'. No Van Allen, Hugo, Riaz, Gide or other of the 12 mentioned. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): Rodig 2018 CheckMate 064; Chen PL 2016 (MDACC). URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6961655/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/CCL5-CXCL9_Dangaj.csv | Caveats: outcome_guided=yes because the CCL5hi/CXCL9hi cut-offs that define the groups (from which the 21 genes were selected by differential expression) were chosen by looking at non-ICB survival curves; no ICB outcome used for gene selection. Online June 2019 (predates Jung, Liu, Braun, Puch, Limagne1). The Key Resources Table (lung/colon/breast dataset IDs) was not in the local text; the text describes them as survival (RFS/OS) collections, not ICB cohorts.

development_data: Own MSKCC NSCLC single-cell CITE/RNA/TCR-seq (4 ICB-naive specimens): genes DE in CD39hi vs other CD8+ T cells; filtered to T/NK-expressed genes using independent NSCLC scRNA-seq (Wu 2021 Nat Commun); refined by Spearman R>0.5 correlation with ENTPD1 in OAK bulk RNA-seq (expression only). Tested in OAK (atezolizumab vs docetaxel).
evidence: STAR Methods 'Clinical outcomes analyses': 'A gene expression signature suitable for estimation of CD39+ CD8+ T cells from bulk RNA-seq of NSCLC tumors was derived by first identifying genes that were differentially expressed by CD39hi CD8+ T cells from the human scRNAseq dataset... we filtered against independent NSCLC scRNA-seq data57 [Wu 2021] to only select genes expressed in the T/NK cell compartment... We further refined the signatures by selecting genes that were well correlated with ENTPD1 (Spearman R >0.5) in bulk NSCLC tumor RNA-seq from the OAK clinical trial42.' Results 'CD39 expression on CD8+ T cells portends benefit from ICB therapy': 'we derived a 23-gene signature score of CD39+ CD8+ T cells from our lung cancer single cell dataset... to evaluate whether this was predictive of benefit from ICB in a dataset of baseline tumor transcriptomes of patients with NSCLC who were randomized to docetaxel chemotherapy or atezolizumab ICB in the phase III OAK clinical trial41,42' (median / top-quartile splits). Other ICB data NOT among the 12: OAK (refs 41 Mazieres 2021 JTO, 42 Patil 2022 Cancer Cell) and own MSKCC flow-cytometry cohort (23 stage IV ICB-monotherapy patients; %CD39+ of CD8+ by flow, not the gene signature). Not POPLAR, not Jung. Braun appears only as co-author of a review (ref 20, Gohil 2021); Riaz (ref 5) and Sade-Feldman (ref 8) cited only as background ('Total CD8+ T cell content alone is not a reliable predictor'). No GEO/ENA ICB cohort accessions used. Sources: local txt/36574773.txt (PMC9887636, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9887636/), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/CD39-CD8Tcell_Chow.csv (23 genes incl. ENTPD1, CXCL13, PDCD1, ZNF683). | Caveats: Gene selection used OAK expression (ENTPD1 correlation) but not OAK outcomes; OAK outcome then tested (= C-type use of OAK, not among the 12). Paper online Dec 2022 (Immunity 2023), after all 12 cohorts, but none used.

development_data: Own scRNA-seq (Smart-seq2) of 16,291 CD45+ cells, 48 biopsies / 32 ICB-treated melanoma patients: unsupervised k-means clustering of CD8+ T cells into CD8_G (memory-like) vs CD8_B (exhausted-like); CD8_G = 34 marker genes (Table S2)
evidence: Signature definition: Results 'Clustering all CD8+ T cells (n=6,350) revealed 2 major cell states: CD8_G with increased expression of genes linked to memory, activation and cell survival (e.g. IL7R, TCF7, REL, FOXP1, FOSL2 and STAT4)'; 'CD8_G cells were enriched in responding lesions (2-sided Wilcoxon p=1.4e-6)' (own cohort; markers via cluster DE, Fisher's exact, Bonferroni q<=0.05). STAR Methods 'Whole transcriptome analysis of bulk tumor samples': 'We used bulk RNA-seq data from the Van Allen et al. (n=37) and Riaz et al. (n=51) datasets ... To compute the bad and good signature scores we computed the average expression of each set of marker genes (CD8_G=34 genes, CD8_B=1114 genes, Table S2)' (bhklab list = 34 genes). Use was EXPRESSION ONLY: Discussion 'signatures of CD8_G and CD8_B, as well as known markers of T cell states ..., are equally correlated with CD3 transcript number in samples from these cohorts (Figure S7)'; no response/survival analysis in Van Allen or Riaz. Independent validation of the claim used TCF7/CD8 immunofluorescence in an own anti-PD-1 cohort (33 pts, 43 samples) - not among 12. Hugo, Prat, Snyder etc. only cited. URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6641984/ | Caveats: Van Allen and Riaz are marked V only in the sense that the frozen CD8_G score was computed there (correlation with CD3); their outcomes were NOT analysed, so they did not validate predictive performance and their outcome data were not used. Treat as 'used, expression only, no outcome' (could equally be shown as blank for outcome-independence purposes). Gene selection itself was unsupervised (clustering), but the choice of CD8_G as the 'good' state came from its association with lesion response in the authors' own scRNA cohort (not among 12).

development_data: Non-ICB tumour microarray datasets (multiple cancer types): top 25 genes correlated with 'total functional aneuploidy' (expression-derived)
evidence: Carter et al. Nat Genet 2006 (local txt 16921376.txt = Nature Genetics landing page: abstract + reference list only; full text paywalled, not read). Abstract: 'We developed a computational method to characterize aneuploidy in tumor samples based on coordinated aberrations in expression of genes localized to each chromosomal region... total functional aneuploidy. We identified a signature of chromosomal instability from specific genes whose expression was consistently correlated with total functional aneuploidy in several cancer types. Net overexpression of this signature was predictive of poor clinical outcome in 12 cancer data sets representing six cancer types.' Thus genes were ranked by correlation with an expression-derived aneuploidy score in non-ICB tumour microarray data; clinical outcome (survival, non-ICB) was used to evaluate, not (per abstract) to select genes. Published 2006, predates all 12 ICB cohorts and ICB therapy; no ICB data. bhklab https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/CIN25_Carter.csv: 25 genes. | Caveats: outcome_guided = no based on abstract only (Methods not accessible); confidence medium for that field, high for the all-blank cohort calls (2006 predates all cohorts).

development_data: Differential expression NB vs CB in Van Allen 2015 ipilimumab RNA-seq (n=35 of 40); TCGA SKCM used for co-expression/methylation characterisation only
evidence: D for Van_Allen: Results 'From a previously reported cohort of 110 melanoma patients treated with ipilimumab, we analyzed the 40 with associated tumor-derived RNA-seq data ... A differential gene expression analysis comparing NB (n=22) and CB (n=13) groups identified 457 genes upregulated in NB samples ... 7 of the top 12 genes overexpressed in NB samples were clustered within a 75 kb region of chromosome Xq28 ... All 8 genes ... which we refer to as anti-CTLA-4 Resistance associated MAGE-A (CRMA) genes'; STAR Methods 'Study Design': DE between CB and NB (two-fold, one-sided Wilcoxon p<=0.05); 'our discovery cohort'. Survival (KM, Cox) also in same cohort. Validation (not among 12): 'independent, validation cohort comprised 41 patients from the CheckMate 064 trial (Weber et al., 2016) treated with ipilimumab followed by nivolumab'; only 5 CRMA genes (MAGEA3, MAGEA2, MAGEA2B, MAGEA12, MAGEA6) available there = the 5-gene bhklab list. V for Hugo: 'Anti-PD-1 cohort 1 comprised 28 pre-anti-PD-1-treated tumors (Hugo et al., 2016)'; Results 'we found none of these genes to associate with clinical outcome to PD-1 blockade, suggesting the specificity of the CRMA signature to ipilimumab outcome (Figure 3E) (Hugo et al., 2016)' (frozen gene set tested; negative/specificity result). Anti-PD-1 cohort 2 = nivolumab-then-ipilimumab arm of CheckMate 064 (not among 12). Riaz 2017 not used ('Riaz et al., 2016' cited = SERPINB3 Nat Genet paper). Other ICB cohorts not among 12: CheckMate 064 (both arms). URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6044280/ | Caveats: bhklab CRMA list (5 MAGE-A genes) is the subset measurable in the CheckMate 064 validation data; the 8-gene CRMA locus was selected by outcome in Van Allen. Hugo is a specificity test (signature NOT expected to predict anti-PD-1 response), still a frozen-signature test -> V.

development_data: Predefined CTL marker set (CD8A, CD8B, GZMA, GZMB, PRF1; cited Rooney 2015) used as CTL level in TIDE; TIDE dysfunction/exclusion signatures built from non-ICB data (TCGA/PRECOG/METABRIC survival interaction tests; CAF/MDSC/M2-TAM profiles from GEO)
evidence: CTL genes predefined: Results 'we used the average expression level of CD8A, CD8B, GZMA, GZMB and PRF1 to estimate the cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) level in a tumor16' (ref 16 = Rooney 2015); Methods 'The CTL level is estimated through the bulk-tumor expression average of CD8A, CD8B, GZMA, GZMB and PRF1'. TIDE built on non-ICB data ('TIDE is trained using data from ICB-naive tumors'). ICB testing ('Performance comparison on predicting ICB response'): 'We collected the RNA-Seq data in melanoma for anti-CTLA4 [ref 3 = Van Allen 2015] and anti-PD1 [ref 14 = Hugo 2016] ... 25 and 42 pre-treatment tumors' (Fig. 4a,b: 25 anti-PD1 Hugo; 42 anti-CTLA4 Van Allen) and NanoString anti-PD1 (ref 15 = Prat 2017, not among 12); CTL-high/low split 'Tumors with all positive values (higher than average) are classified as CTL-high'. CTL alone evaluated: SI Supplementary Table 8b 'Comparison between T-cell exclusion signature and CTL' (AUC CTL: PD1 RNASeq [Hugo] 0.59, CTLA4 RNASeq [Van Allen] 0.77, NanoString 0.64); 'CD8' (CD8A+CD8B) biomarker in Supp. Table 7/8a. Riaz: Results 'a recent study generated RNA-Seq profiles on another melanoma cohort treated with anti-PD1 45 [ref 45 = Riaz 2017]. We focused on 24 patients ... ipi-naive'; SI Supp. Fig. 6 (24 ipi-naive, 26 ipi-progressed). Threshold note: SI Supp. Fig. 5c 'The TIDE prediction performance with different CTL thresholds ... Our current CTL cutoff corresponds to the method one (All) with zero as the threshold' - a sensitivity analysis on the ICB cohorts (Hugo, Van Allen, Prat); paper states the cutoff is robust, no statement that it was chosen on these data. TIDE score scaling uses SD of correlations in TCGA melanoma (non-ICB); KM split at TIDE >1 vs <1. Other ICB cohorts not among 12: Prat 2017 NanoString; Nathanson 2017 (SERPINB9 survival only). Mariathasan (ref 24) only cited. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6487502/ ; https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41591-018-0136-1/MediaObjects/41591_2018_136_MOESM1_ESM.pdf | Caveats: For the CTL gene set itself all three cohorts are frozen-signature tests (V). Caveat: the CTL-high/low cutoff ('all five above average') was shown robust in Supp. Fig. 5c on Hugo/Van Allen/Prat; if a reviewer treats that comparison as tuning, Hugo/Van Allen could be argued D for TIDE's CTL cutoff, but the text does not say the cutoff was selected from it. TIDE's dysfunction signature used TCGA/PRECOG/METABRIC overall survival (non-ICB clinical outcome) - relevant to TIDE, not to the 5 CTL genes.

development_data: TCGA (12 tumour types, 5255 samples): cytotoxic CD8+ T/NK marker genes (table S5B), 'similar to the one utilized in Rooney et al.', excluding pan-cancer amplified/deleted genes; scored as mean rank expression
evidence: Davoli et al. Science 2017 (PMC5592794; local txt 28104840.txt). Methods 'Immune signature and cell cycle signature score': 'For the cytotoxic immune signature, we utilized a set of genes representing molecular markers of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and NK cells, similar to the one utilized in Rooney et al. (29)... genes that are significantly amplified or deleted in a pan-cancer analysis (3) were excluded' - defined/scored in TCGA only, no outcome used. ICB data: Results 'SCNA levels predict survival of melanoma patients after immunotherapy': 'We analyzed a data set derived from a recent clinical trial of anti-CTLA-4 blockade in metastatic melanoma patients (27)' [ref 27 = Van Allen 2015, PMID 26359337] - SCNA level from WES (VarScan2), mutation/neoantigen load; long-term survival vs no benefit (Fig. 6C), Cox HR=2.24 (Fig. 6D-E); 'we performed a similar analysis in another data set derived from an independent clinical trial of anti-CTLA-4 blockade (Fig. 6F,G) (26)' [ref 26 = Snyder/Chan NEJM, not among 12]. Van Allen RNA-seq (RNA-SeQC RPKM) was used for a DIFFERENT gene set: 'a gene expression signature derived from the TCGA data set (23 genes; table S6E) ... positively correlated with aneuploidy and negatively correlated with the immune infiltrate was associated with worse survival in melanoma patients treated with immunotherapy (HR=2.2; P=0.05) (27)'. The main text never reports the 7-gene cytotoxic immune signature itself being tested against ICB outcome in Van Allen (or any ICB cohort). Supplement (tables S5/S6) could not be accessed (PMC/EuropePMC supplementary links blocked, science.org 403). Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5592794/ | Caveats: Judgement call on Van_Allen: the CYT genes were NOT chosen with Van Allen data and, per the main text, the CYT score was not outcome-tested there. 'C' is assigned conservatively because Van Allen is the discovery ICB cohort for the paper's immunotherapy claim (aneuploidy/immune-evasion -> poorer anti-CTLA-4 survival; Snyder used as confirmation), and its RNA-seq outcome was used for the related 23-gene immune-anticorrelated signature. A strict reading (signature never evaluated in Van Allen) would make it blank. Other 11 cohorts not used (Riaz etc. published later; Hugo not used). bhklab lists association='resistance' for CYT_Davoli, which conflicts with the biology (cytotoxic signature is reduced in aneuploid tumours; expected to favour response) - check direction. bhklab genes https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/CYT_Davoli.csv (CD247, CD2, CD3E, GZMH, NKG7, PRF1, GZMK) assumed = table S5B (not verified; supplement inaccessible). | Reconciliation: Van_Allen changed from C (first reading, low confidence) to blank: the 7-gene CYT score was defined in TCGA and is never tested against ICB outcome in the paper; Van Allen 2015 was used only for SCNA level and a separate 23-gene SCNA/immune set (table S6E). Borderline: treat as C only if a reviewer counts any ICB cohort used in the paper. (first reading coded Van_Allen=C)

development_data: 12-chemokine GES from an earlier CRC metagene (Coppola 2011, Am J Pathol, 326 CRCs; unsupervised metagene); applied to 14,492 Moffitt solid tumours and 120 stage IV melanoma metastases (Affymetrix), linked to ectopic lymph-node-like structures by histology
evidence: Messina et al. Sci Rep 2012 (PMC3479449; local txt 23097687.txt). Results: 'We had earlier identified in colorectal cancer a unique 12-chemokine (CCL2, CCL3, CCL4, CCL5, CCL8, CCL18, CCL19, CCL21, CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, and CXCL13) GES from a metagene grouping with overwhelming enrichment for immune-related and inflammation-related genes (11)' [ref 11 = Coppola 2011, PMID 21703392; Europe PMC abstract: 'Metagene analysis with gene chip technology was performed on 326 CRCs'; the 12-chemokine subset correlated with TL-ELNs and survival]. In this paper the score is PC1 of the 12 genes (Methods 'mRNA microarray analysis') in Moffitt tumours; survival association in 10 melanoma patients (Table 1). Only ICB mention: one long survivor had received ipilimumab. Discussion: 'We plan to evaluate the capacity of the 12-chemokine GES to predict ... response to immune checkpoint inhibitory antibodies'. Paper (2012) predates all 12 cohorts. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3479449/ | Caveats: No ICB cohort used. Gene set defined by expression metagene (non-outcome) in CRC; survival associations were tested after definition (Coppola 2011 not read in full; abstract only).

development_data: Literature-derived 'classic' EMT genes (refs incl. Mak 2016, Byers 2013, Lou 2016) kept if expressed above 10 reads in the authors' own single-centre UPenn NSCLC cohort (52 pts, 2nd-line anti-PD-1/PD-L1, AmpliSeq transcriptome); score = sum z(AGER, FN1, MMP2, SNAI2, VIM, ZEB2) minus sum z(CDH1, CDH3, CLDN4, EPCAM, MAL2, ST14); tested only in that cohort.
evidence: Methods 'Study Design and Patients': 'single-center, retrospective, observational study ... at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania'; 52 pts with usable RNA. Methods 'Gene Signature Generation': 'The goal of this study was to validate existing signatures from the literature in our independent patient population ... There is not yet a validated lung cancer EMT signature, so we prospectively generated a gene list based on previous publications ... Selected genes had levels of expression that were clearly above baseline (using a cutoff of 10 reads in our data set).' Hugo (ref 15) is cited only as the source of the IPRES gene list, and Mariathasan (ref 19) only as the source of the TGF-beta genes (TGFB1, TGFBR2, ACTA2, COL4A2, TAGLN); no data from those cohorts were analysed. Kim (gastric) is not mentioned (the only 'Kim' is a KEYNOTE-010 co-author). No public ICB dataset used. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own UPenn NSCLC cohort (n=52). URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7176049/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/EMT_Thompson.csv | Caveats: The gene filter used the own cohort's expression, not its outcome. The combined weighted score (-0.60*EMT + 0.19*inflammation) was fitted by logistic regression on response in the own cohort, but it is not the SignatureSets EMT_Thompson (unweighted +/-1). Online Oct 2019 (predates Liu, Braun, Puch, Limagne1).

development_data: TCGA BLCA (muscle-invasive UC, cystectomy, n=408): 18 MSigDB hallmark-EMT genes most associated with overall survival conditional on T-cell infiltration (bivariate Cox, Wald p<1e-6); stromal origin supported by UC PDX mouse/human read separation
evidence: Methods 'Survival analysis': 'To obtain the EMT/Stroma_core gene list, we assessed the association of each individual EMT gene with OS while controlling the effects of ITA using the bivariate Cox regression model ... We used a stringent cutoff of p < 1e-6 to select 18 EMT/Stroma_core genes' (TCGA; bhklab list = these 18 genes). ICB cohort: CheckMate 275 (nivolumab, metastatic UC, n=214 biomarker cohort, HTG EdgeSeq; only 8 of 18 genes on panel: FLNA, EMP3, CALD1, FN1, FOXC2, LOX, FBN1, TNC) - not among the 12; claim: CD8 IHC x EMT/Stroma_core interaction with response/PFS/OS. Mariathasan/IMvigor210 NOT analysed: only cited in Discussion ('Recently, using data from a large phase 2 study of patients with metastatic UC treated with the PD-L1 inhibitor atezolizumab, Mariathasan et al demonstrated that a lack of response was associated with a signature of TGF-b signaling ... derived from fibroblasts40'). No other ICB cohorts. URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6115401/ | Caveats: Outcome guidance = TCGA overall survival after cystectomy (non-ICB clinical outcome). None of the 12 cohorts used; ICB evidence comes solely from CheckMate 275 (8-gene subset).

development_data: Immune GEP previously developed in the GeparSixto neoadjuvant chemotherapy (+/- carboplatin) TNBC/HER2+ trial (Denkert JCO 2015, PMID 25534375): predefined panel of immune-activating/suppressive mRNAs (CXCL9, CCL5, CD8A, CD80, CXCL13, IDO1, PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA4, FOXP3; IGKC/CD21 also measured), all predictive of pCR under chemotherapy. Karn 2020 applied it (predefined analysis) to RNA-seq of 149 GeparNuevo TNBC (durvalumab vs placebo + chemo); median GEP split.
evidence: Abstract (PubMed/Europe PMC): 'We obtained both whole exome sequencing and RNA-Seq data from pretreatment samples of 149 TNBC of the recent neoadjuvant ICB trial, GeparNuevo. In a predefined analysis, we assessed the predictive value of TMB and a previously developed immune GEP for pathological complete remission (pCR)... When we stratified patients in groups based on the upper tertile of TMB and median GEP...'. Crossref reference list (29 refs): GEP source ref 24 = Denkert 2015 JCO (GeparSixto TILs and immune genes); the only one of the 12 cohort papers cited is Van Allen 2015 (ref 8), within a block of TMB-and-ICB background refs (5 Le 2017 MMR, 6 Snyder 2014, 7 Rizvi 2015, 8 Van Allen 2015, 9 Samstein 2019, 10 Cristescu 2018) - apparently cited as background evidence that TMB predicts ICB response, not as analysed data. Denkert 2015 abstract: 'mRNA expression of immune-activating (CXCL9, CCL5, CD8A, CD80, CXCL13, IGKC, CD21) as well as immunosuppressive factors (IDO1, PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA4, FOXP3) was measured in 481 tumors... All 12 immune mRNA markers were predictive for increased pCR.' Other ICB cohort used (NOT among the 12): GeparNuevo (durvalumab, TNBC). Sources: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:32461104, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.annonc.2020.05.015, Europe PMC abstract of PMID 25534375, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/GeparSixto_Karn.csv (10 genes). | Caveats: COULD NOT READ FULL TEXT: annalsofoncology.org, sciencedirect and repository mirrors returned 403/connection refused. The abstract restricts the analysis to GeparNuevo; Van Allen's citation context inferred from the reference cluster, not read. outcome_guided 'unclear': genes were an a priori immune panel in GeparSixto; whether the 10-gene subset/weighting was chosen using GeparSixto chemotherapy pCR (non-ICB outcome) was not verifiable.

development_data: KEYNOTE-001 melanoma pembrolizumab (19-pt pilot + 62-pt confirmatory), NanoString 680-gene panel; refined 6-gene IFN-gamma signature
evidence: Ayers et al. JCI 2017 (PMC5531419; local txt 28650338.txt; Table 2 image https://www.jci.org/articles/view/91190/table/2). All data are Merck pembrolizumab trials on a NanoString 680-gene panel: Results 'a set of baseline biopsies from 19 patients with metastatic melanoma enrolled in the KEYNOTE-001 study ... was used as a pilot data set'; 'confirmed using expression data from an additional cohort of 62 patients with metastatic melanoma treated with pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-001'; refined signatures tested in KEYNOTE-012 HNSCC (n=40/43) and gastric (n=33); final GEP from 'KEYNOTE-012 (bladder, gastric, HNSCC, and TNBC) and KEYNOTE-028 (anal canal, biliary, colorectal, esophageal, and ovarian)' (n=220) and validated in 96 PD-L1-unselected HNSCC from KEYNOTE-012. No public cohort (Hugo, Van Allen or any of the 12) is mentioned anywhere in the text; Riaz/Gide/Kim/Mariathasan etc. were published after this paper (JCI online June 2017). Other ICB cohorts used (not among the 12): KEYNOTE-001 melanoma, KEYNOTE-012, KEYNOTE-028. Gene-set identity: bhklab IFN_Ayers = IDO1, CXCL10, CXCL9, HLA-DRA, STAT1, IFNG = exactly the refined 'IFN-gamma (6-gene)' signature of Table 2. Derivation (Results): 10-gene 'preliminary IFN-gamma' signature built from top genes by 1-sided t test responders vs non-responders in the 19-pt pilot; then 'refined by removal of genes that did not reach a nominal 1-sided P value less than 0.05 for positive association with either objective response or PFS in the confirmatory set of 62 melanoma tumors, yielding refined IFN-gamma (6-gene)'. Then tested in KEYNOTE-012 HNSCC and gastric. | Caveats: Outcome-guided development entirely in KEYNOTE-001 (non-public); gastric validation was KEYNOTE-012 (n=33), not the Kim/Samsung cohort. bhklab file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/IFN_Ayers.csv (weights all 1; paper scored as mean of log10 quantile-normalised genes).

development_data: Neuroblastoma (SEQC NB RNA-seq, Su 2014): hill-climbing feature selection of 15 pairwise checkpoint-gene relations separating spontaneous regression vs high-risk progression (108 samples, age<18 mo, PC2+PC3>0 cluster); candidate pool = 28 checkpoint genes from literature measured in all RNA-seq datasets
evidence: Development on non-ICB data: Online Methods 'Feature selection and IMPRES construction on the NB data' ('hill climbing aggregative feature selection involving 500 iterations of a five-fold cross validation procedure'); SI Supplementary Methods details (13 vs 3 samples per class train/test, binomial p<0.05 on score_f -> 15 features). Main text: 'We then turned to apply IMPRES to predict melanoma patients' response to ICB, without any further training' and 'IMPRES is constructed only once from the NB data and never trained on any melanoma dataset'. V cohorts: Fig. 2A 'ROC curves quantifying IMPRES prediction AUC across numerous publically available ICB response datasets1-6' with refs 1 = Van Allen 2015, 3 = Hugo 2016, 6 = Riaz 2017 (pre and on nivolumab); Table 1 lists Van Allen, Hugo, TCGA SKCM, Chen, Prat, Riaz, MGH. Other ICB cohorts not among 12: Chen PL 2016 (NanoString, anti-CTLA-4/anti-PD-1), Prat 2017 (NanoString), TCGA SKCM ICB-treated subset, new MGH cohort (GSE115821; 31 anti-PD-1, 10 anti-CTLA-4). Possible concerns checked: (i) 'we focus on 28 genes that were measured in all RNA-sequencing datasets analyzed in this paper' - expression/platform availability, not outcome; (ii) 'IMPRES can capture almost all true responders while misclassifying less than half of the non-responders (at threshold = 8)' - threshold described on the aggregate 297-sample compendium incl. Hugo/Riaz/Van Allen (Fig. 2C-D), descriptive; (iii) 'Feature reduction analysis' (11-feature subset) and 'Training a predictor using melanoma datasets' (Riaz+Hugo; Hugo+Van Allen) are comparator/exploratory analyses, not the published 15-feature IMPRES; (iv) CDP pathway analysis of responders vs non-responders in datasets 1,3,4,6 is interpretive. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6693632/ ; https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41591-018-0157-9/MediaObjects/41591_2018_157_MOESM1_ESM.pdf | Caveats: outcome_guided=yes refers to NB clinical outcome (spontaneous regression vs high-risk progression), not ICB outcome. The suggested 'threshold = 8' was read off aggregate ICB data including Hugo/Riaz/Van Allen; if a downstream evaluation uses that fixed cutoff rather than the continuous 0-15 score, those cohorts are not independent for the cutoff. Ref 4 in the PMC/SI list is 'Weinstein TCGA Pan-Cancer' (TCGA SKCM ICB-treated subset per Table 1). Nathanson, Gide, Liu not used (Gide/Liu postdate).

development_data: Pooled anti-PD-1 melanoma ICB discovery cohort (Riaz17 n=51, Gide19 n=41 PD-1 mono, Hugo16 n=28; total 120). Per-dataset one-sided t-test of PD vs PR/CR on expression normalized to the Ayers 10-gene IFN-g score, restricted to 770 NanoString IO360 genes, p-values combined by Pearson's method, top 18 genes = IMS. TCGA used only for descriptive/prognostic analyses.
evidence: Results 'Definition of an immunosuppression signature': 'three external datasets14,15,21 [Hugo, Riaz, Gide] of advanced melanoma treated with an anti-PD-1 ICI with response and RNA-seq data, which we used as our discovery cohort (n = 120)... We then identified 18 genes of which the expression levels, after adjusting for IFN-g signature score, are consistently associated with negative response to ICI in the discovery cohort as our IMS'; Fig 1A-C volcano plots by response 'on Riaz17 (n = 51), Gide19 (n = 41) and Hugo16 (n = 28)'. Methods 'Identification of the IMS genes': one-sided t-test PD vs PR/CR after IFN-g normalization, IO360 770 genes, 'p-values from the three datasets in the discovery cohort were then combined using Pearson's method... top 18 genes were identified as our IMS genes'. Methods 'External data sources': 'For the Gide19 and Liu19 studies, only baseline data from samples that received anti-PD-1 monotherapy... were used'. VALIDATION: Results: 'We next tested the prediction ability of IFN-g/IMS in a newly generated RNA-seq dataset from 55 tumor tissues of melanoma patients treated with anti-PD-1 monotherapy at Peking University Cancer Hospital (PUCH)' (AUC 0.81); 'In the public dataset of 54 ... melanoma treated with anti-PD-1 (Liu1913)' AUC 0.66; 'two publicly available RNA-seq datasets ... anti-CTLA-4 therapy (VanAllen15; n = 42)40 and metastatic gastric cancer ... anti-PD-1 therapy (Kim18; n = 45)41' AUC 0.75/0.82; Abstract calls PUCH 'a newly generated internal validation cohort (n = 55)' and the others 'three published datasets'. Refs: 13=Liu 2019 Nat Med (PMID 31792460), 14=Hugo 2016, 15=Riaz 2017, 21=Gide 2019, 40=Van Allen 2015, 41=Kim 2018. PUCH = Peking University Cancer Hospital, Beijing; Data availability (PMC XML): 'raw sequence data from PUCH dataset ... deposited in the Genome Sequence Archive ... under accession number HRA000524'; ORCESTRA ICB_Puch record (zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7332226) cites this paper (PMID 33542239). No other ICB cohorts beyond these 7 (Table 2). Sources: local txt/33542239.txt (PMC7862369, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7862369/), dl/pmc/33542239.xml, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/IMS_Cui.csv (18 genes, matches IMS list), dl/bhk/orcestra_icb.json. | Caveats: bhklab IMS_Cui = the 18 IMS genes only (FAP, PDGFRB, CD163, SIGLEC1, IL10, CCL2, CCL8, CCL13, INHBA, VCAN, AXL, TWIST2, ADAM12, COL6A3, STC1, ISG15, BCAT1, OLFML2B); the paper's predictor is the IFN-g/IMS ratio (Ayers 10-gene IFN-g, PMID 28650338, predefined). Caveats: (1) a robustness 'randomized permutation test' re-derived IMS from 3 randomly chosen of all 7 datasets (Riaz, Gide, Hugo, PUCH, Liu, Van Allen, Kim) 35 times - a sensitivity analysis, not the published gene list, so validation cohorts kept as V; (2) Youden-index cutoffs for ORR/KM were optimized within each cohort including validation cohorts (AUCs are threshold-free; no universal cutoff proposed) - kept V for PUCH/Liu/Van_Allen/Kim. Gide D used only the anti-PD-1 monotherapy subset (n=41); Liu subset n=54 (anti-PD-1 mono baseline); Riaz n=51 (ipi-naive/ipi-progressed mix not specified). Puch is the paper's own cohort: its first use was as validation.

development_data: KEYNOTE-001 melanoma pembrolizumab (19 + 62 pts), NanoString; refined 'expanded immune (18-gene)' signature
evidence: Ayers et al. JCI 2017 (PMC5531419; local txt 28650338.txt; Table 2 image https://www.jci.org/articles/view/91190/table/2). All data are Merck pembrolizumab trials on a NanoString 680-gene panel: Results 'a set of baseline biopsies from 19 patients with metastatic melanoma enrolled in the KEYNOTE-001 study ... was used as a pilot data set'; 'confirmed using expression data from an additional cohort of 62 patients with metastatic melanoma treated with pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-001'; refined signatures tested in KEYNOTE-012 HNSCC (n=40/43) and gastric (n=33); final GEP from 'KEYNOTE-012 (bladder, gastric, HNSCC, and TNBC) and KEYNOTE-028 (anal canal, biliary, colorectal, esophageal, and ovarian)' (n=220) and validated in 96 PD-L1-unselected HNSCC from KEYNOTE-012. No public cohort (Hugo, Van Allen or any of the 12) is mentioned anywhere in the text; Riaz/Gide/Kim/Mariathasan etc. were published after this paper (JCI online June 2017). Other ICB cohorts used (not among the 12): KEYNOTE-001 melanoma, KEYNOTE-012, KEYNOTE-028. Gene-set identity: bhklab IRG_Ayers (17 genes: CD3D, IDO1, CIITA, CD3E, CCL5, GZMK, CD2, HLA-DRA, CXCL13, IL2RG, NKG7, HLA-E, CXCR6, TAGAP, CXCL10, STAT1, GZMB) = the refined 'expanded immune gene signature' (18 genes) of Table 2 MINUS LAG3. Derivation: 28-gene 'preliminary expanded immune' set built from genes correlated with the preliminary IFN signature that had 'nominal P value less than 0.05 for positive association with objective response and/or PFS on the initial set of 19 melanoma tumors', then refined to 18 genes by removing genes not reaching P<0.05 for ORR/PFS in the 62-pt confirmatory melanoma set. | Caveats: bhklab IRG_Ayers omits LAG3 (Table 2 lists 18 genes incl. LAG3) - curation discrepancy, possibly a mapping loss. Not to be confused with the final 18-gene T cell-inflamed GEP. bhklab file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/IRG_Ayers.csv.

development_data: TCGA-CESC only (non-ICB): ImmPort immune-related genes, differentially expressed tumour vs normal (edgeR), then univariate Cox for OS in a TCGA training split, LASSO-Cox, and multivariate-Cox coefficients (11 genes), validated on the TCGA test split. The ICI link is inferred only from TCIA immunophenoscores and PD1/CTLA4 expression in TCGA.
evidence: Methods 'Development and validation of the immune related signature for CC': 'The Cancer Genome Atlas CC patients were divided into a training set and a testing set ... a univariate Cox proportional hazard regression analysis was used to identify the relationship between DE IRGs and OS in the training set ... LASSO'. Results 'Construction of immune related risk signature': risk score = 0.32196*LEPR - 0.64921*PRLHR - 0.32677*NR2F2 + 0.23573*PRL + 0.39005*NRP1 + 0.02975*TNFRSF10B + 0.39830*TNFRSF10A + 0.14607*PLAU - 0.68625*IFI30 + 0.38166*ANGPTL5 - 0.03522*IGF1. Results 'The immune related risk signature and response to ICI': only IPS from TCIA. Availability: data only from TCGA, ImmPort, TCIA. No ICB-treated cohort was used (no Van Allen, Hugo or IMvigor210); Hugo 2016 is cited only in the Discussion (ref 55) as biomarker literature. Other ICB cohorts used: none. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6844304/ (local txt from PMC HTML) ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/IRG_Yang.csv | Caveats: outcome_guided=yes means TCGA-CESC overall survival (non-ICB). IMPORTANT for scoring: the SignatureSets weights (-1/+1) follow the tumour-vs-normal direction (LEPR, PRLHR, NR2F2, PRL, NRP1, ANGPTL5, IGF1 = -1; TNFRSF10B, TNFRSF10A, PLAU, IFI30 = +1), not the published Cox coefficients. Signs disagree for LEPR, PRL, NRP1, ANGPTL5 (positive Cox, -1 in SignatureSets) and IFI30 (negative Cox, +1). Also, the published score is a poor-prognosis risk score (low risk = higher IPS), so SignatureSets' 'sensitive' label may be inverted relative to the paper.

development_data: scRNA-seq of ICB-treated melanoma (Sade-Feldman GSE120575; responder vs nonresponder cell-cluster proportions -> TREM2hi macrophages, Tgd_c21 gamma-delta T cells, B_c22 B cells) combined with bulk RNA-seq outcome data of Hugo GSE78220 (cancerclass) to build the 108-gene ImmuneCells.Sig.
evidence: Hugo = D. Results 'The development of an ICT outcome signature': 'we developed an ICT responsiveness signature based on the scRNA-seq dataset and a bulk gene expression dataset - GSE782209 using the cancerclass R package23. This signature had significantly high prognostic values for ICT outcomes in the discovery dataset. Specifically, for the GSE78220 dataset (N = 28, NR vs R: 13 vs 15), the signature had an AUC ... of 0.98'; Fig. 4a legend: 'the initial discovery dataset - GSE78220'; Methods 'Study design': 'For the development of the ICT outcome signature, we analyzed the transcriptome-level gene expression data set (GSE78220) of an immune checkpoint therapy (ICT) study9' (ref 9 = Hugo Cell 2016). Peer-review file (reviewer): 'A neosignature named ImmuneCells.Sig ... integrating scRNA variations and bulk RNA data from a previous analysis (GSE78220) was defined. Unsurprisingly it was well correlated to the outcome when tested on the patients from the GSE78220 since this data was used to create the signature.' Riaz/Gide/Liu = V: 'To validate the above ICT response signature - ImmuneCells.Sig, we analyzed three independent gene expression datasets ... For the first two datasets (GSE91061 and PRJEB23709)10,11, the pretreatment melanoma samples were selected for validation. Neither of these datasets were used to develop the ImmuneCells.Sig.' Third validation dataset = 'MGSP' dbGaP phs000452.v3.p1, 103 pretreatment anti-PD-1 samples, ref 12 = Liu D Nat Med 2019 (peer-review file also cites 'Liu et al. Nat Med. 2019' for N=103), i.e. Liu, not Van Allen. Hugo and Riaz were also used to test a separate 40-gene TREM2hi macrophage set (Supplementary Fig. 7b,c). Other ICB data (not among 12): Sade-Feldman GSE120575 scRNA (cell-population discovery, outcome-based), Jerby-Arnon GSE115978 scRNA and Yost GSE123813 BCC scRNA (validation of cell states). Sources: (PMC7545100, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7545100/); supplementary + peer-review files via https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7545100/supplementaryFiles (, moesm2.txt, Supplementary Data 9 = 108 genes); code https://github.com/donghaixiong/Immune_cells_analysis (Fig4_signature_analysis.R) | Caveats: Important caveat for the V cohorts: the authors' code (Fig4_signature_analysis.R) fits a cancerclass nearest-centroid predictor ('fit(..., method = "welch.test")') and predicts on the SAME dataset in each validation cohort (BMS038/GSE91061, PRJEB23709 73 samples, NatMed 103 samples). So the published 'validation' AUCs (0.96/0.86/0.88) are resubstitution estimates with centroids/weights re-trained on each cohort's outcomes; only the 108-gene list was frozen. The text also derives treatment-specific z-score thresholds (0.19 and 0.1) from the Gide anti-PD-1 and combo subsets ('In the model built from Pre-anti-PD-1 dataset...'). Because the SignatureSets/GSVA implementation uses only the gene list (from Hugo + scRNA), I coded Riaz/Gide/Liu as V; a strict reading of the D definition ('train/tune the model', 'choose thresholds') applied to the original paper's classifier would make them D. Exactly how genes were selected from Hugo is not fully described (the code in the repo starts from the final ImSig.rds list), but the text and reviewer state that Hugo outcome data were used to create it; many signature genes (e.g. ASPM, BIRC5, CLDN7, GRIA1, MUSK) are not immune-cell markers, consistent with bulk DE selection in Hugo.

development_data: Predefined literature gene list (cytolytic, HLA, IFN-gamma pathway, chemokines, adhesion molecules; 'immunologic constant of rejection' refs 45,46); geometric mean on NanoString in own MDACC sequential anti-CTLA-4 -> anti-PD-1 melanoma cohort (n=56)
evidence: Roh et al. Sci Transl Med 2017 (PMC5819607; local txt 28251903.txt). Results: 'The immune score was defined as the geometric mean of gene expression in selected genes including cytolytic markers, HLA molecules, IFN-gamma pathway, selected chemokines, and adhesion molecules related to tumor rejection in the context of the immunologic constant of rejection (45,46)'; Methods lists the 41 genes (= bhklab). In own MDACC cohort it was correlated with TCR clonality (fig. S5B) and CNA loss burden (fig. S12B), not with response. Van Allen use (Methods 'Independent (Van Allen) cohort analysis'): 'WES data (SAM files) from 110 melanoma patients and RNA-seq data from 42 patients ... downloaded through the dbGaP (phs000452.v2.p1)' - used to validate copy-number-loss burden vs CTLA-4 response (Fig. 3A, P=0.016). For the immune score: 'Immune scores for the independent cohort were calculated by ESTIMATE'; CNA loss vs ESTIMATE immune score r=-0.41 (fig. S12A); 'Our immune scores and those calculated by ESTIMATE (table S16) showed a strong positive correlation (0.91) in the independent cohort (fig. S12C)'. No association of the Roh immune score with ICB response/survival is reported in Van Allen. Hugo (ref 25) cited only in Introduction. Own cohort = ORCESTRA ICB_Roh (not among the 12). Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5819607/ | Caveats: Van_Allen marked V because the frozen gene set was applied to Van Allen RNA-seq expression (table S16) only for concordance with ESTIMATE and CNA correlation; Van Allen OUTCOME was used for CNA-burden analyses, not for the immune score. Could be argued blank (no outcome test of this signature). Genes were not outcome-selected.

development_data: Non-ICB: 16 public advanced serous ovarian cancer cohorts (>2,200 tumours; GEO/ArrayExpress/TCGA). From 782 immune-cell marker genes (Charoentong/TCIA) + antigen-presenting genes, 76 genes prognostic for favourable overall survival by per-cohort Cox + fixed-effects meta-analysis (P<0.02, FDR<0.1); gene weights from meta-analysis HR and SE. Outcome used = OS (mostly after platinum chemotherapy).
evidence: Methods 'Immune score': 'The prognostic evaluation of immune marker genes and antigen-presenting genes was determined by Cox proportional hazards regression analysis in the 16 cohort datasets of ovarian cancer... In total, 76 genes were identified to be significantly prognostic of favorable outcome... the HR and the standard estimates (SE) of HR were used to determine the weight of a marker gene in immune score.' Results 'Immune score predicts response to immunotherapy': 'We first tested the prognostic value of immune score in the four immunotherapy datasets with transcriptome data released (9, 35-37). These include three melanoma datasets received anti-CTLA-4 or anti-PD-1 therapy and an urothelial cancer datasets received anti-PD-L1 therapy. A meta-analysis of the four datasets shows that the immune score is significantly associated with favorable survival in immunotherapy datasets (Fig. 5A; HR = 0.73 [0.57-0.93], P = 0.01). Significantly prolonged survival was observed for high vs. low immune score patients in the combined melanoma cohort (Fig. 5B)... 28 (41.2%) responders ... in the high score group of the four datasets, and only 19 (26.8%) ... in the low score group (P = 0.077)'; Suppl Fig S8: ROC/KM in 'the cohort received anti-CTLA-4 immunotherapy' [Van Allen]. Reference mapping (AACR HTML reference list): 9 = Van Allen EM, Science 2015; 35 = Hugo W, Cell 2016; 36 = Snyder A, PLoS Med 2017 (urothelial atezolizumab - NOT Mariathasan); 37 = Riaz N, Cell 2017. Other ICB cohort NOT among the 12: Snyder 2017 urothelial. Sources: local txt/29661778.txt and dl/html/29661778.html (AACR, https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-17-3862), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/ImmunoScore_Hao.csv (76 genes). | Caveats: Signature frozen on ovarian OS data (no ICB data in gene selection/weights), so no D. The ICB claim (abstract: 'immune score is a strong predictor of ... the response to immunotherapy') arises jointly from a symmetric fixed-effects meta-analysis of the four ICB datasets (+ pooled melanoma KM), with no separate ICB discovery/validation split -> C per the symmetric-meta-analysis rule; if the matrix treats any test of a signature frozen on non-ICB data as validation, these three become V. Exact Riaz/Hugo/Van Allen sample subsets and per-cohort HRs are in Fig 5A (not in text). Published Aug 2018 (online Apr 2018), so later cohorts (Gide, Liu, Kim, Jung, Braun, Mariathasan, Miao, Puch, Limagne1) could not be or were not used (Kim/Mariathasan/Miao published before final print but not used). | Reconciliation: per the coding rule that development on non-ICB data rules out D/C, cohorts in which a signature frozen on non-ICB data was only tested are coded V; C is kept only where analysis of the cohort itself motivated/shaped the signature. Van_Allen/Hugo/Riaz changed from C to V: the 76-gene weighted immune score was fixed on ovarian (non-ICB, overall survival) data, then "tested" in four ICB datasets (Van Allen, Hugo, Riaz, Snyder 2017) with a meta-analysis HR=0.73. BORDERLINE: these cohorts are where the ICB claim was first made (no ICB discovery/validation split). (first reading coded Van_Allen=C, Hugo=C, Riaz=C)

development_data: 27-gene inflammation score 'based on a previously published gene score' (ref 14 = Ayers et al., JCI 2017); unweighted sum of log2 z-scores; tested in the authors' own UPenn NSCLC anti-PD-1/PD-L1 cohort (n=52). The Ayers source genes came from pembrolizumab KEYNOTE-001 melanoma data (genes associated with response, plus genes correlated with that IFN-gamma signature).
evidence: Methods 'Gene Signature Generation': 'Our inflammation signature was based on a previously published gene score14 and created by summing (unweighted) log2 Z scores for 27 inflammation related genes (Supplemental Table 1).' Ref 14 = Ayers M et al. IFN-gamma-related mRNA profile predicts clinical response to PD-1 blockade, JCI 2017 (PMID 28650338). Ayers (local txt 28650338): the 'preliminary expanded immune' 28-gene set was made from genes correlated with a preliminary IFN-gamma signature, itself chosen as genes with 'nominal P value less than 0.05 for positive association with objective response and/or PFS' in 19 KEYNOTE-001 melanoma tumours. The only test was in the own UPenn cohort (Results: responders vs non-responders, 6.0 vs -5.5, p=0.014, AUC 0.69). None of the 12 cohorts' data used; Hugo and Mariathasan are cited only as gene-list sources for other signatures (IPRES, TGF-beta). Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own UPenn NSCLC cohort (n=52); upstream KEYNOTE-001 (Ayers). URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7176049/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5531419/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/Inflammatory_Thompson.csv | Caveats: outcome_guided=yes refers ONLY to the upstream Ayers derivation (KEYNOTE-001 pembrolizumab outcomes, not among the 12); Thompson themselves selected no genes by outcome. The 27 genes overlap the Ayers 28-gene list but also include PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4, CXCL11, ITGAL, PTPRC etc.; Thompson Supplemental Table 1 was not checked, so exactly how they adapted it is unverified.

development_data: Non-ICB human melanoma expression: genes up-regulated in the top-KDM5A-expression quartile (or positively correlated with KDM5A) in TCGA SKCM RNA-seq (n=473; 1193 genes) intersected with the Leeds Melanoma Cohort microarray (n=703 primary melanomas; 93 genes) -> 8 genes (KDM5A, RIOK1, MVB12B, HMCN1, FAM13C, PDE1A, IKZF3, ANO3). No outcome used for gene selection. Mouse B16/MC38 KDM5A-overexpression experiments are mechanistic only.
evidence: Results 'A KDM5A gene signature is associated with therapeutic response...': 'To delineate a KDM5A gene signature, we analyzed RNA-seq data of 473 cutaneous melanoma samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) project (15) and identified differentially expressed genes that were up-regulated in the quartile with the highest expression of KDM5A. We then integrated 1193 genes from the TCGA skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) cohort and 93 genes from the LMC that were positively correlated with KDM5A expression. We identified eight intersecting targets ... and defined this eight-gene set as a KDM5A gene signature (Fig. 1C).' 'We tested the utility of this KDM5A gene signature in predicting responses to anti-PD-1 therapy ... We analyzed RNA-seq data from two large published cohorts ...: the Liu et al. (16) cohort (n = 121) and the Riaz et al. (17) cohort (n = 32).' 'We built predictive models of the response to ICB using the KDM5A gene signature in each cohort and compared their predictive accuracy' (Fig. 1E legend: 'Mean cross-validation AUC scores'); AUC 0.65 (Liu) and 0.63 (Riaz). Liu is the main-figure cohort (Fig. 1D-G; KM split at the 75% quantile of S-score; pre-treatment subset n=104 in fig. S1D-G); Riaz in fig. S1B-C. Ref 16 = Liu D Nat Med 2019 (n=121, anti-PD-1); ref 17 = Riaz N Cell 2017. Hugo, Gide, Van Allen are neither analysed nor cited (OpenAlex reference list checked). Other cohorts used (not among 12): TCGA SKCM and Leeds Melanoma Cohort (development, non-ICB). Sources: full-text PDF of Sci Transl Med 12:eaax2282 obtained from the Internet Archive copy of the Peking University lab site (https://web.archive.org/web/20240413224352id_/http://gene.pku.edu.cn/media/publication/papers/eaax2282.full.pdf -> ); abstract https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32908002/; science.org (https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/scitranslmed.aax2282) returned HTTP 403; references via https://api.openalex.org/works/pmid:32908002 | Caveats: Main text read in full; the Supplementary Materials and Methods (bioinformatic details, data file S2, fig. S1) were NOT accessible (science.org 403), so preprocessing of Liu/Riaz, the Riaz subset definition (n=32; pre- or on-treatment unknown) and the CV model type are unverified. C/V boundary judgement: the 8-gene set was frozen from non-ICB data (TCGA/LMC) before ICB testing, so Liu/Riaz did not shape the genes. I coded C (not V) because Liu and Riaz are the paper's only ICB cohorts, were analysed in parallel ('in each cohort', models with cross-validation fitted within each cohort), and are where the ICB-response claim was first established. Change to V if the matrix uses V for any frozen-signature test. Liu (phs000452, n=121, anti-PD-1) is clearly Liu 2019, not Van Allen 2015. | Reconciliation: per the coding rule that development on non-ICB data rules out D/C, cohorts in which a signature frozen on non-ICB data was only tested are coded V; C is kept only where analysis of the cohort itself motivated/shaped the signature. Liu/Riaz changed from C to V: the 8 genes were fixed from TCGA SKCM + Leeds Melanoma Cohort (non-ICB, KDM5A co-expression) before ICB testing. BORDERLINE: Liu and Riaz are the paper's only ICB cohorts; prediction models were fitted with cross-validation within each cohort (supplementary methods not accessible). (first reading coded Liu=C, Riaz=C)

development_data: Own CHA Bundang NSCLC anti-PD-1 cohort (n=21, 9 DCB vs 12 NDB; GSE136961 = ORCESTRA ICB_Hwang, not among the 12): pre-existing gene sets (GO BP, immune landscape, immunoscore, hallmark, MSigDB C7 immunologic) scored by ssGSEA on a 393-gene multiplex panel and selected by random forest (LOOCV) for discriminating DCB vs NDB. M1 = GSE5099 M1 vs M2 set; peripheral T cell = GSE7852 LN vs FAT Tconv up (panel-covered genes).
evidence: Results 'Major gene signatures associated with therapeutic response': 'From the results of random forest analysis of the gene signature data, we identified two major gene signatures (GS) showing marked expression differences depending on the response to ICI and named each signature as the M1 signature and peripheral T cell signature' (own 21-patient cohort). Methods 'Random forest and gene signature analysis': random forest with LOOCV over five gene-set collections. Riaz = V: Discussion: 'When we compared our results with other ICI-treated, non-NSCLC cohort to validate our study, we found the mRNA data of 51 pre-ICI treated melanoma patients and its clinical outcome by Riaz et al.24 ... The results of PSMB9, M1 signature and peripheral T cell signature were also similar to ours, showing higher expression in responsive group, but not statistically significant.' (ref 24 = Riaz N, Cell 2017, PMID 29033130). 'Jung' occurs only as an author name (Hee Jung An, joint supervisor), not the Jung 2019 Samsung cohort; Mariathasan (ref 27) is cited only for TGF-beta biology; Richard 2019 (ref 26, Dijon nivolumab exome) cited only. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own CHA NSCLC cohort (discovery). Sources: (PMC6971301, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6971301/) | Caveats: Riaz used only post hoc in the Discussion as a confirmatory check of the already-selected signatures (non-significant trend); no gene or threshold choice came from Riaz. outcome_guided=yes because the two sets were picked from thousands of candidate gene sets by an outcome-supervised random forest in the own cohort (gene content itself = predefined MSigDB sets restricted to panel genes).

development_data: Own Liu cohort (144 anti-PD-1 melanoma; 121 RNA-seq). Gene set predefined: all 13 MHC-II HLA genes (HLA-DMA ... HLA-DRB5), ssGSEA score; association with response discovered in this cohort (strongest in the ipilimumab-pretreated subgroup); tested in Riaz as validation.
evidence: Results: 'expression of all 13 MHC-II-associated HLA genes was higher in responders (collective two-sided binomial test, P = 0.0002; Fig. 2g)'; 'A composite, rank-based score of MHC-II HLA expression (single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA)43; Methods) was higher in responders than in progressors in the overall cohort and the subgroup treated with ipilimumab ... (P = 0.03, P = 0.03 and P = 0.31)'; 'We found very similar results in the largest available independent validation cohort44 ... although the difference was not significant in this smaller cohort (n = 32 ...)' (Fig 3f-h). Methods 'Validation': 'we used the remaining cohort44 as our primary validation cohort ... uveal and ocular melanomas were excluded (Riaz cohort, n = 5 excluded) ... data were obtained from https://github.com/riazn/bms038_analysis'. Extended Data Fig 10b: MHC-II-only model in the Riaz ipilimumab-treated subgroup (n=23) gave AUC 0.65 (empiric P = 0.21). Ref 44 = Riaz, Cell 2017. Hugo (ref 20) was considered but not used (no prior-ipilimumab information). Van Allen is cited only in the Introduction. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6898788/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/MHC-II_Liu.csv | Caveats: C, not D, for Liu: the gene list is a predefined gene family, not filtered by outcome. However, the MHC-II score was the top feature in outcome-driven forward selection for the Liu ipilimumab-treated logistic model (with LDH and lymph-node metastasis) and was median-split in Fig 4; that model is not the SignatureSets signature. Riaz=V: the frozen gene set was tested there (non-significant).

development_data: Own Liu cohort (144 anti-PD-1 melanoma; 121 RNA-seq). Gene set predefined from biology: MHC-I HLA genes HLA-A/B/C/E/F plus TAP1, TAP2, B2M, scored by ssGSEA; its association with response was examined in this cohort.
evidence: Methods 'GSEA and ssGSEA': 'we generated ssGSEA projections for gene sets using rank normalization, including ... MHC-I HLA genes (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-E, HLA-F, TAP1, TAP2 and B2M)'. Results: 'MHC-I antigen-presentation genes all trended toward having higher expression in responders (collective two-sided binomial test, P = 0.02; Fig. 2g ...)'; TAP2 or HLA-A/B/C amplifications were found exclusively in responders (Fisher P = 0.001); Fig. 2h: 'An immune-related cluster of MHC-I- and MHC-II-related gene expression is observed, with subclusters of MHC-I and MHC-II genes' (correlation clustering of response-associated features). Abstract: novel features 'predicted selective response, including features associated with MHC-I and MHC-II antigen presentation'. Methods 'Validation': Riaz (ref 44) was the primary validation cohort, but only MHC-II score, heterogeneity and Hallmark GSEA were tested there (Fig 3f-j, Extended Data Fig 10); no MHC-I score result in Riaz is reported. Hugo (ref 20) was considered but not used ('did not have information on previous ipilimumab treatment'); Roh 2017 was considered but not used; Van Allen 2015 (ref 10) is only cited in the Introduction. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6898788/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/MHC-I_Liu.csv | Caveats: C, not D: the genes were not chosen by outcome. The 'cluster' in the SignatureSets description refers to the Fig 2h feature-correlation cluster, not to gene selection. The MHC-I expression evidence in Liu was weak (a trend; no single gene significant). Riaz is left blank for this signature because the paper reports no MHC-I score test in Riaz, though Riaz data were used in the paper. dbGaP phs000452 is shared with Van Allen, but Van Allen data were not analysed.

development_data: Four syngeneic UV-induced/GEM mouse melanoma models (anti-CTLA-4-resistant M1/M2 vs sensitive M3/M4): DE genes (t-test, DESeq2) ranked, then stepwise gene addition chosen by Fisher's exact test of response prediction in the Van Allen ipilimumab cohort -> 45 genes (33 up, 12 down); score = sum(+1 up, -1 down) of FPKM, z-scored.
evidence: Methods 'MPS development': 'Our gene selection approach started from choosing the two most upregulated genes and stepwise adding the next most upregulated gene and using the sum of gene expression as a score to classify patient samples in the Van Allen dataset4. We used Fisher's exact test to evaluate the performance of our classifier in predicting patient response to treatment. We chose the largest gene list that had a P value <0.05 as derived from Fisher's exact test and identified 27 upregulated genes using this approach.' Results: 'Based on differential gene expression statistics and sequential evaluation of response prediction in the Van Allen dataset4 by Fisher's exact test, we identified a 45-gene signature'; 'MPS scores correctly predicted the response of 81% of patients using the 33rd percentile as a cutoff' (Van Allen). Hugo/Riaz = V: 'To confirm the ability of MPS to predict ICB efficacy, we compiled baseline RNA-seq data of immunotherapy-naive patients from two metastatic melanoma cohorts treated with anti-PD-1 (Hugo and Riaz datasets9,13). Nonresponder melanomas consistently exhibited significantly higher MPS scores' (Extended Data Fig. 9; pooled 'Hugo-Riaz' dataset also used for ROC vs TIDE/PD-L1/TMB). Ref 4 = Van Allen Science 2015 (PMID 26359337); ref 9 = Riaz Cell 2017; ref 13 = Hugo Cell 2016. Van Allen expression was also used for immune-cell signature/CIBERSORT comparisons with the mouse models. Gide, Liu and others not mentioned. Other ICB data: mouse models (anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-1). Sources: (PMC8482620, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8482620/) | Caveats: Only the Riaz ipilimumab-naive subset was used. The 33rd-percentile cut-off was also chosen in Van Allen. Liu (Dec 2019) predates this paper (Apr 2020) but was not used.

development_data: Literature candidate markers filtered by marker-like co-expression (pairwise similarity) in TCGA RNA-seq (24 datasets, 9986 samples, 32 tumour types); checked vs flow/IHC in ovarian cancer
evidence: Danaher et al. JITC 2017 (PMC5319024; local txt 28239471.txt). Methods: candidate markers 'primarily drawn from [7]' (Bindea) and [9]; selection by 'pairwise similarity statistic between all pairs of the cell type's candidate marker genes within each of 24 TCGA RNASeq datasets'; Table 1 Macrophages: '33 candidates, 4 selected, mean similarity 0.71: CD68, CD84, CD163, MS4A4A' (= bhklab). Only ICB data: 'A recent clinical trial collected biopsies from melanoma patients through checkpoint inhibitor therapy, first before and during anti-CTLA4 therapy and then before and during anti-PD1 therapy [31] ... publically available NanoString data from 54 of these biopsies' [ref 31 = Chen PL et al. Cancer Discov 2016, MDACC - NOT among the 12]. TCGA survival analyses were done after marker selection. None of the 12 cohorts is mentioned. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5319024/ | Caveats: Other ICB cohort (not among 12): Chen PL 2016 MDACC NanoString (54 biopsies). Paper (Feb 2017) predates all of the 12 except Hugo and Van Allen, neither used.

development_data: MCP-counter (Becht 2016) 'Myeloid dendritic cells' gene set (CD1A, CD1B, CD1E, CLEC10A, CLIC2, WFDC21P), predefined from non-ICB expression specificity; Helmink only applied MCP-counter in its own ICB cohorts (MDACC neoadjuvant melanoma, OpACIN-neo, MDACC RCC) and in TCGA.
evidence: Methods 'Deconvolution of the cellular composition with MCP-counter': MCP-counter applied to give abundance scores for eight immune cell types including 'myeloid dendritic cells'. Supplementary Table 3 (MCP-Counter geneset) 'Myeloid dendritic cells' = CD1A, CD1B, CD1E, CLEC10A, CLIC2, WFDC21P, identical to the SignatureSets list. Supplementary Table 13: FDR for myeloid DC by response = 0.45 (neoadjuvant baseline), 0.8 (on-treatment), 0.089 (RCC baseline), 0.15 (OpACIN). None of the 12 cohorts is mentioned or used in the paper. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): MDACC neoadjuvant melanoma NCT02519322, OpACIN-neo NCT02437279, MDACC RCC NCT02210117. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8762581/ ; https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-019-1922-8/MediaObjects/41586_2019_1922_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/Myeloid-DC_Helmink.csv | Caveats: The gene set is MCP-counter's, not Helmink's own. My computation from Supp Tables 4 and 6 gives median myeloid-DC MCP scores HIGHER in responders (neoadjuvant baseline 0.26 vs -0.07; on-treatment 0.29 vs -0.39; OpACIN 0.14 vs -0.60). The SignatureSets annotation ('resistance'; 'more expressed in non-responders') is therefore not supported by the paper material I read; the main text makes no specific myeloid-DC claim.

development_data: Mouse E0771 orthotopic breast cancer bilateral 'resection and response' model treated with anti-PD-1: bulk RNA-seq of sorted CD8+ TILs at day 15, DESeq2+sva responder vs nonresponder mice (padj<0.05, FC>1.5) -> 85 responder-up and 69 nonresponder-up genes (mouse-to-human ortholog mapping). Human checks: METABRIC breast cancer survival (non-ICB), TIDE run on mouse profiles, GSEA overlap with Sade-Feldman scRNA CD8 activation/exhaustion signatures.
evidence: SI Appendix Methods: 'A mouse-derived early-therapeutic-stage responder signature was defined as the 85 genes that were upregulated in the responders. A mouse-derived early-therapeutic-stage non-responder signature was defined as the 69 genes that were upregulated in the non-responders.' Main text 'Mouse-Derived Responder and Nonresponder Gene Signatures Are Predictive of Patient Survival and Response to ICB': human analyses were METABRIC survival ('because comprehensive BC response to ICB datasets is not yet available'), TIDE applied to the mouse RNA-seq, and 'We explored a melanoma patient-derived single-cell RNA-seq dataset (25) and found a significant association between our responder and nonresponder signatures with the melanoma patient-derived CD8+ T cell activation and exhaustion signatures' (ref 25 = Sade-Feldman Cell 2018) via GSEA. Mariathasan (ref 43) is cited only for CXCR3-ligand biology; no Hugo/Riaz/Van Allen/Gide/Liu data. The SI Appendix (pnas.2002806117.sapp.pdf, downloaded from Europe PMC supplementary files for PMC7519254) contains no bulk human ICB cohort analysis. Other ICB data (not among 12): mouse anti-PD-1 model (development), Sade-Feldman scRNA-derived signatures (comparison only). Sources: (PMC7519254, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7519254/); https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7519254/supplementaryFiles -> | Caveats: No bulk human ICB cohort was analysed despite the main text saying 'bulk RNA-seq from BC and melanoma patient samples'; the 'melanoma' arm is a GSEA comparison against published Sade-Feldman scRNA signatures. SignatureSets' description ('validated there signature in published ICB cohorts') overstates this. outcome_guided=yes refers to MOUSE anti-PD-1 response (responder vs nonresponder mice), not human outcomes. The 'human-adjusted' signatures (METABRIC correlation expansion) are separate from the mouse-derived 85/69-gene sets.

development_data: No data-driven development: Nishino 2017 is a narrative review of PD-L1 IHC as a biomarker; TIDE (Jiang 2018) used 'PD-L1 gene expression as the IHC surrogate' as a predefined comparator. The 3-gene set (CD274, PDCD1LG2, PDCD1) is a curation construct
