evidence: bhklab https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/PDL1_Nishino.csv = CD274, PDCD1LG2, PDCD1. Nishino et al. Nat Rev Clin Oncol 2017 (PMC5650537; local txt 28653677.txt) is a review; section 'PD-L1 and other immune-checkpoint molecules' discusses PD-L1 IHC in trials (nivolumab phase I, KEYNOTE etc.); no gene-expression signature, no PDCD1LG2/PD-L2 mRNA, no dataset analysis. TIDE (Jiang et al. Nat Med 2018; PMC6487502; local txt 30127393.txt; Supplementary PDF https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41591-018-0136-1/MediaObjects/41591_2018_136_MOESM1_ESM.pdf): Supplementary Table 7 'PDL1: An immunohistochemistry (IHC) biomarker approved by FDA [ref 5 = Nishino]. In this study, we used the PD-L1 gene expression as the IHC surrogate'; Methods: 'The predicted values of gene expression biomarkers (for example, IFNG, CD8, PDL1 and CRMA) were the average values among all members defined by the original publications'. PDL1 was evaluated as a comparator in Fig. 4d-i / Supp Table 8a: anti-PD1 RNA-seq melanoma n=25 [ref 14 = Hugo 2016] AUC 0.62; anti-CTLA4 RNA-seq melanoma n=42 [ref 3 = Van Allen 2015] AUC 0.62; anti-PD1 NanoString n=33 [ref 15 = Prat 2017, not among 12] AUC 0.42; and Supp Fig. 6a,b Riaz [ref 45] ipi-naive n=24 and ipi-progressed n=26 (PDL1 among compared biomarkers). No outcome-driven gene selection. Not used: Mariathasan, Gide, Braun, etc. (TIDE paper text has no urothelial/RCC/gastric ICB data). | Caveats: Gene-set origin: neither cited paper defines a 3-gene CD274+PDCD1LG2+PDCD1 set; TIDE's PDL1 comparator was PD-L1 (CD274) expression alone (single gene). The bhklab 3-gene set appears to be a curation choice, so the V entries refer to TIDE's evaluation of CD274 expression, not of the exact 3-gene set. Strictly, the 'original paper' (Nishino review) used no cohorts at all (all blank); V entries come from 30127393 which the curation also cites. Other ICB cohort used in TIDE: Prat 2017 NanoString (and Nathanson for SERPINB9 only).

development_data: Own Lund population-based melanoma cohort (n=169, non-ICB; Illumina HT12, GSE65904): SAM (FDR=0, FC>1.5) contrasting IHC-defined MITFlow/PTENneg tumours vs other melanomas -> 276-gene centroid (mean expression in MITFlow/PTENneg); classification by Pearson cor>0.2 to centroid.
evidence: Methods 4.3: 'To determine genes with significantly different expression between MITFlow/PTENneg tumors and other melanomas, we used significant analysis for microarray (SAM)... To create the centroid, the average expression value across MITFlow/PTENneg tumors was obtained for each of the 276 genes. The centroid was subsequently applied to external datasets... All samples with a cor. >0.2 were classified as transcriptionally similar'. 'The ICB treated RNA-seq datasets [18,20] were downloaded from PRJEB23709 and https://github.com/riazn/bms038_analysis' (ref 18 = Riaz Cell 2017; ref 20 = Gide Cancer Cell 2019). Results 2.4: 'Next, we used two melanoma patient cohorts treated with ICB... The first cohort included RNA sequencing data from pre-treatment tissue samples of 69 patients receiving either anti-PD1 monotherapy or anti-PD1/CTLA4 combination therapy [= Gide]... The second cohort consisted of 42 patients receiving anti-PD1 monotherapy [= Riaz]... We then combined both cohorts and found that patients with MITFlow/PTENneg classified melanomas were associated with inferior patient survival independent of study population (HR = 1.9; 95%CI 1.1-3.2, p = 0.03, multivariate Cox analysis, Figure 5C).' Hugo, Van Allen and Liu are not mentioned (the only 'Liu' is an author in ref 4, Peng 2016). Other cohorts used (not among 12): Lund GSE65904 (development, non-ICB), Yan 2019 vemurafenib +/- cobimetinib cohort (BRAF/MEK inhibitors, non-ICB). Sources: (PMC7140048, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7140048/) | Caveats: C/V boundary judgement: the centroid and the cor>0.2 cut-off were frozen from the non-ICB Lund cohort before ICB testing, so neither Gide nor Riaz outcomes shaped genes, weights or threshold. I coded C (not V) because Gide and Riaz are the paper's only ICB cohorts and were pooled symmetrically into the single analysis that established the ICB-outcome claim (no earlier ICB discovery cohort). Change both to V if the matrix keeps C only for cohorts with cohort-specific discovery analyses. In-text citation numbers for the two ICB cohorts are garbled ([20,21], [20]); the Methods accession list resolves them (PRJEB23709 = Gide, bms038 = Riaz). The MITFlow/PTENneg phenotype was chosen for signature building because it was associated with poor survival in the Lund cohort (non-ICB OS), but genes were selected by IHC-group contrast, not outcome; hence outcome_guided=no. | Reconciliation: per the coding rule that development on non-ICB data rules out D/C, cohorts in which a signature frozen on non-ICB data was only tested are coded V; C is kept only where analysis of the cohort itself motivated/shaped the signature. Gide/Riaz changed from C to V: the 276-gene centroid and cor>0.2 cut-off were frozen in the non-ICB Lund cohort (GSE65904) before the ICB survival analysis. BORDERLINE: Gide+Riaz were pooled for the single analysis that established the ICB claim. (first reading coded Gide=C, Riaz=C)

development_data: Mouse E0771 orthotopic breast cancer bilateral 'resection and response' model treated with anti-PD-1: bulk RNA-seq of sorted CD8+ TILs at day 15, DESeq2+sva responder vs nonresponder mice (padj<0.05, FC>1.5) -> 85 responder-up and 69 nonresponder-up genes (mouse-to-human ortholog mapping). Human checks: METABRIC breast cancer survival (non-ICB), TIDE run on mouse profiles, GSEA overlap with Sade-Feldman scRNA CD8 activation/exhaustion signatures.
evidence: SI Appendix Methods: 'A mouse-derived early-therapeutic-stage responder signature was defined as the 85 genes that were upregulated in the responders. A mouse-derived early-therapeutic-stage non-responder signature was defined as the 69 genes that were upregulated in the non-responders.' Main text 'Mouse-Derived Responder and Nonresponder Gene Signatures Are Predictive of Patient Survival and Response to ICB': human analyses were METABRIC survival ('because comprehensive BC response to ICB datasets is not yet available'), TIDE applied to the mouse RNA-seq, and 'We explored a melanoma patient-derived single-cell RNA-seq dataset (25) and found a significant association between our responder and nonresponder signatures with the melanoma patient-derived CD8+ T cell activation and exhaustion signatures' (ref 25 = Sade-Feldman Cell 2018) via GSEA. Mariathasan (ref 43) is cited only for CXCR3-ligand biology; no Hugo/Riaz/Van Allen/Gide/Liu data. The SI Appendix (pnas.2002806117.sapp.pdf, downloaded from Europe PMC supplementary files for PMC7519254) contains no bulk human ICB cohort analysis. Other ICB data (not among 12): mouse anti-PD-1 model (development), Sade-Feldman scRNA-derived signatures (comparison only). Sources: (PMC7519254, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7519254/); https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7519254/supplementaryFiles -> | Caveats: No bulk human ICB cohort was analysed despite the main text saying 'bulk RNA-seq from BC and melanoma patient samples'; the 'melanoma' arm is a GSEA comparison against published Sade-Feldman scRNA signatures. SignatureSets' description ('validated there signature in published ICB cohorts') overstates this. outcome_guided=yes refers to MOUSE anti-PD-1 response (responder vs nonresponder mice), not human outcomes. The 'human-adjusted' signatures (METABRIC correlation expansion) are separate from the mouse-derived 85/69-gene sets.

development_data: DLBCL (10 public microarray datasets, 2030 cases): genes most correlated with focus gene STAT1 across datasets (Care 2015 Additional file 4, STAT1 sheet, top 39 by NumDataSets^MedianRho); later used unchanged by Zemek 2019 (mouse AB1/Renca ICB models + human ICB cohorts)
evidence: Gene definition: Care et al. Genome Med 2015 (PMC4566848; local txt 26362649.txt), 'Focus gene analysis': per dataset Spearman correlations merged by median across 11 DLBCL datasets; Additional file 4 (https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1186%2Fs13073-015-0218-3/MediaObjects/13073_2015_218_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx), sheet 'STAT1': the top 39 ranked genes (STAT1, GBP1, IRF1, WARS, RARRES3, CXCL9, GBP5, LAP3, APOL3, IDO1, GBP4, LAG3, CXCL10, GZMA, PRF1, IFNG, GBP2, CCR5, SLC31A2, APOL6, CXCL11, SERPINA1, FCGR1B, TNFSF10, GZMK, CST7, FGL2, TAP1, SERPING1, FCER1G, CD2, GIMAP4, IFIT3, CCL4, CXCR6, GIMAP5, XAF1, SLAMF7, ANKRD22) match bhklab https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/STAT1_Care.csv exactly in order (WARS=WARS1, RARRES3=PLAAT4). No ICB data in Care. ICB use: Zemek et al. Sci Transl Med 2019 (author manuscript read from UWA repository https://api.research-repository.uwa.edu.au/ws/files/51959451/Zemek_et_al._2019.pdf; science.org not accessible). Methods: 'The STAT1 signature was derived from Care et al. (31), defined based on variance-ranked Spearman correlations of gene expression across 11 DLBCL datasets'. Results: 'there was a significant (p 0.019) enrichment of a STAT1 signature in responsive tumors from the urothelial cancer/atezolizumab cohort (23) [Mariathasan 2018, IMvigor210] as well as in a second cohort of patients with melanoma treated with nivolumab (p 0.044) (22) [Riaz 2017] (fig. 2F, fig. S5)'; Fig. 2F = GSEA CR vs PD in IMvigor210 (n=192); fig. S5B = Riaz GSEA CR+PR (10) vs PD (23), 'We also tested the STAT1 signature in a second cohort'. Survival analysis (Methods): 'leveraged RNAseq data from the Imvigor210 trial (23), available as an R data package (Imvigor210CoreBiologies) ... two prototype vectors were defined ... a responder prototype from radiological complete responders and partial responders and a progressor prototype based on progressor samples ... This decision score was used to classify all patients'; high STAT1 activation -> longer OS (fig. S5C). Hugo (24) and Van Allen (10) cited only in Introduction. | Caveats: Mariathasan = C: gene set was predefined (DLBCL correlation, no ICB outcome), but the paper's human ICB association was first/mainly shown in IMvigor210 (main Fig. 2F), with Riaz as the 'second cohort' (supplement) -> V. Caveat: Zemek's IMvigor210 survival classifier used responder/progressor centroids computed from IMvigor210 response labels (outcome-trained scoring in the same cohort), so a stricter reading could code Mariathasan as D for that analysis; the bhklab unweighted gene set itself is unaffected. Read the submitted/accepted manuscript version, final published text not checked (science.org 403). Gide (Feb 2019) not used. Other ICB data: mouse AB1, Renca, AE17, B16 models (GSE117358). | Reconciliation: per the coding rule that development on non-ICB data rules out D/C, cohorts in which a signature frozen on non-ICB data was only tested are coded V; C is kept only where analysis of the cohort itself motivated/shaped the signature. Mariathasan changed from C to V: Zemek 2019 took the predefined Care 2015 STAT1 gene set (DLBCL, non-ICB) to test a hypothesis from mouse models; IMvigor210 was the first human test (GSEA CR vs PD). BORDERLINE: Zemek's IMvigor210 PFS analysis used a CABS classifier whose responder/progressor reference profiles were built from IMvigor210 response labels (outcome-fitted within IMvigor210, but not affecting the unweighted gene list). Source checked: UWA author manuscript https://api.research-repository.uwa.edu.au/ws/files/51959451/Zemek_et_al._2019.pdf (first reading coded Mariathasan=C)

development_data: In vitro: RNA-seq of primary fibroblasts from 6 tissues (bladder PHBR, colon CCD-18Co, breast HMF, lung IMR90, pancreas HPaSteC, ovary HOF) treated with control vs TGF-b1 vs TGF-b1+galunisertib; 19-gene Pan-F-TBRS (non-ICB, non-clinical)
evidence: Supplementary Information (Nature SI PDF, 'Generation of pan-fibroblast TGF-b response signature (Pan-F-TBRS)'): fibroblasts from six tissues 'were serum-starved overnight before treatment with (1) control, (2) TGF-b1 (10ng/mL), or (3) TGF-b1 + Galunisertib ... The Pan-F-TBRS signature was determined using the following criteria: (1) >=2-fold higher in TGF-b1-treated vs controls (FDR 0.1); (2) >=2-fold lower in TGF-b1+inhibitor vs TGF-b1 alone; (3) criteria met in all 6 fibroblast cells. The genes that passed (n = 79) were ranked by strength of inhibition ... and filtered by >=5 CPM mean reduction to define a pan-tissue 19-gene F-TBRS signature.' (bhklab list = 19 genes, consistent). Score = PC1 of z-scored genes within the dataset (unsupervised, 'Signature score computation'). C for Mariathasan (IMvigor210): main text 'To measure TGF-b pathway activity specifically in fibroblasts, we generated a pan-fibroblast TGF-b response signature (Pan-F-TBRS)... the Pan-F-TBRS was significantly associated with non-response in excluded tumours only (Fig. 2d)'; Fig. 2f/ED Fig. 2g GLMs fit in IMvigor210. The motivation came from IMvigor210 outcome analyses (GSEA: cytokine-cytokine receptor set 'the sole feature associated with non-response'; TGFB1/TGFBR2 higher in non-responders), but the genes themselves were selected in vitro, so C not D. No other ICB cohort analysed (Van Allen ref 10 and Hugo ref 32 are only cited; Snyder cited). Other ICB data: none; mouse EMT6/MC38 anti-PD-L1+anti-TGF-b experiments. URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6028240/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25501 ; https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fnature25501/MediaObjects/41586_2018_BFnature25501_MOESM1_ESM.pdf | Caveats: IMvigor210 is the source paper's only patient cohort; the TGF-b hypothesis was outcome-motivated in IMvigor210 (TGFB1/TGFBR2 single-gene association with non-response) even though Pan-F-TBRS gene selection was purely in vitro. All other 11 cohorts: not used (Braun, Gide, Jung, Kim, Limagne1, Liu, Puch postdate Feb 2018; Hugo, Riaz, Van Allen, Miao1 not analysed).

development_data: Predefined 18-gene NanoString Tumor Inflammation Signature (Ayers 2017 / Danaher 2018; proprietary weights) measured on the IO360 beta panel; only tested in the CERTIM cohort (Cochin University Hospital, Paris; 58 pts on anti-PD-1 per label: 37 NSCLC, 10 RCC, 5 melanoma, 4 urothelial, 1 colon, 1 SCLC). TIS genes and weights were originally derived with pembrolizumab outcomes in KEYNOTE-001/-012/-028 (Ayers).
evidence: Methods 'Patients': 'Fifty-eight patients from the CERTIM ... The CERTIM cohort was initiated in our hospital in July 2015 and prospectively includes all the patients treated with a PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor'; Abstract: 'CERTIM cohort is a prospective cohort ... in Cochin University hospital'; ethics 'CPP Ile de France II'. Methods 'Statistical analysis of transcriptional data': 'Gene expression signatures, including the TIS, were calculated as a weighted linear average of the constituent genes [2, 12]. The weighted scores ... are NanoString intellectual property.' Background: TIS 'was demonstrated to retrospectively predict clinical benefit of anti-PD-1 ... in clinical trials [2]' (ref 2 = Ayers 2017). No public ICB dataset and none of the 12 cohorts used; Hugo appears only as a co-author of the cited Zaretsky 2016 paper. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): CERTIM (Paris). URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6829827/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/TIS_Damotte.csv | Caveats: CERTIM is in Paris (Cochin), not Dijon, so it is neither Limagne1 nor Fumet 2018. outcome_guided=yes refers to the upstream Ayers/NanoString derivation (KEYNOTE trials, none among the 12); Damotte did no selection. SignatureSets scores the 18 genes unweighted by GSVA, unlike the proprietary weighted TIS. Published Nov 2019.

development_data: Lund (Skane University Hospital) metastatic melanoma cohort (177 pts IHC; ~160 with gene expression, GSE65904; non-ICB, largely pre-ICB era). Genes chosen by SAM between IHC-defined immune groups: CD8+CD20+ (TLS) vs CD8+ only, and CD8+ only vs immune-poor. The 9 genes up specifically in CD8+CD20+ tumours (asterisked in Extended Data Table 4) form the signature. The CD8+CD20+ group was of interest because of its survival association in the Lund cohort (non-ICB).
evidence: Abstract: 'We derived a gene signature associated with tertiary lymphoid structures, which predicted clinical outcomes in cohorts of patients treated with immune checkpoint blockade.' Fig 3 legend (nature.com figure page): 'a, Heat map of genes specifically upregulated in CD8+CD20+ cases of melanoma ... f, Kaplan-Meier analysis for overall survival in patients treated with anti-CTLA4 (n = 40) ... Data from a previous study 27 [Van Allen] ... g, ... anti-PD1 (n = 69) ... Data from a previous study 22 [Gide] ... h, ... anti-PD1 (n = 40) ... Data from a previous study 28 [Riaz]' (OS P = 0.045, 0.0012, 0.014; trichotomised scores). Extended Data Table 4: 'SAM analysis results to obtain the nine-gene TLS signature' (columns: 'Genes discriminating tumors with CD8 T cells alone compared to immune poor melanomas' and 'Genes discriminating tumors with TLS and CD8 T cells compared to melanomas with CD8 T cells alone'; the 9 genes asterisked). Extended Data Fig 5: c, Riaz survival by ipi-naive/progressed; d, 'Meta Cox regression analysis across the four cohorts treated using ICB (n = 186)' = Danish 37 + Van Allen 40 + Gide 69 + Riaz 40; f, Riaz pre-treatment (n=38) and on-treatment (n=39) TLS score vs RECIST. Extended Data Fig 4a: TLS-signature correlation in Gide baseline (ref 22, n=69). Extended Data Table 5 lists 'Van Allen anti-CTLA4-treated cohort (N=40)', 'Riaz anti-PD1 treated cohort (N=40)', 'Gide anti-PD1 treated cohort (N=61)'. Data availability: PRJEB23709 (Gide), github.com/riazn/bms038_analysis (Riaz), GSE65904, TCGA SKCM, GSE115978, GSE120575. Reporting Summary: 'The derived TLS gene expression signature was firmly validated in several different datasets across multiple gene expression platforms.' Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own Danish anti-CTLA4 cohort (n=37, microarray), Roh 2017 (ref 30; Ext Data Fig 5e), Sade-Feldman GSE120575 and Jerby-Arnon GSE115978 scRNA (B-cell analyses). Non-ICB: Lund cohort, TCGA SKCM metastases (n=349). URLs: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1914-8 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1914-8/figures/3 ; https://media.springernature.com/full/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-019-1914-8/MediaObjects/41586_2019_1914_Tab4_ESM.jpg ; .../41586_2019_1914_Tab5_ESM.jpg ; https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-019-1914-8/MediaObjects/41586_2019_1914_MOESM1_ESM.pdf ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/TLS_Cabrita.csv | Caveats: The main text and Methods are paywalled (no PMC or author manuscript found via Europe PMC, Lund or RegionH portals), so this rests on the abstract, the main Fig 3 legend and image, the Extended Data legends, Extended Data Tables 4-5 (images) and the Reporting Summary. The signature was fixed on non-ICB Lund data before any ICB testing, so Van Allen, Gide and Riaz are V. But the paper's ICB claim rests jointly on these three plus the own Danish cohort (including a pooled meta-Cox), so a strict reading of the joint-claim rule could make them C. Exact SAM thresholds, and whether any survival filter was used, could not be verified. Gide n = 69 in Fig 3g but N = 61 in the Extended Data Table 5 header. The Lund cohort's treatment history was not verified from the Methods.

development_data: Immunopurified endothelial cells from 10 invasive epithelial ovarian cancers vs 5 normal ovaries (Affymetrix U133 Plus 2.0); genes up-regulated >=6-fold in tumour endothelium (Table 1)
evidence: Lu et al. Cancer Res 2007 (local txt 17308118.txt, publisher HTML full text). Results: 'Five normal ovaries and 10 invasive epithelial ovarian cancers were obtained and subjected to negative and positive immunoselection'; 'A multivariate permutation t test (P<0.001) ... identified 1,149 genes that were differentially regulated >=2-fold'; 'Of the 652 genes that were up-regulated >=2-fold, 35 genes were elevated at least 6-fold in tumor endothelium (Table 1)'. The 29 bhklab genes are all in Table 1 (old symbols CSPG2=VCAN, CENTA2=ADAP2, CKLFSF8=CMTM8, HOP=HOPX), i.e. the MSigDB LU_TUMOR_VASCULATURE_UP subset. No clinical outcome and no ICB data; 2007 predates all 12 cohorts. Source: https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/67/4/1757/533976/ | Caveats: Class comparison tumour vs normal endothelium only (non-outcome, non-ICB).

development_data: Own scRNA-seq (33 melanoma tumours, 31 patients, incl. Tirosh 2016) + TCGA SKCM bulk (n=473): malignant-cell genes correlated with CD8 T-cell signature OE across TCGA bulk tumours (seed), expanded by co-variation across single malignant cells; refinement with Patel 2017 CRISPR co-culture screen
evidence: Definition (STAR Methods 'Linking cell states to tumor composition'): seed exclusion signatures = 'top 20 malignant genes that are significantly negatively (positively) correlated' with T-cell OE across bulk tumours; final program = genes correlated with seeds across single malignant cells; 'we applied the approach to our clinical scRNA-seq melanoma data and bulk RNA-Seq data of 473 Skin Cutaneous Melanoma (SKCM) tumors from TCGA'. The 'refinement' (STAR Methods 'The immune resistance program'): 'We further refined the immune resistance program by integrating the scRNA-seq data with the results of a genome-scale CRISPR screen (Patel et al., 2017)' - not an ICB cohort. Post-treatment program (part of the union resistance program) = post-ICI-resistant vs untreated malignant cells in own scRNA cohort. V cohorts (Results 'The Resistance Program Predicts ICI Responses'): 'three published cohorts of less than 50 patients each (Hugo et al., 2015 [sic]; Riaz et al., 2017; Van Allen et al., 2015)'; 'In 27 melanoma patients treated with pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) (Hugo et al., 2016), underexpression of the program pre-treatment distinguished the five complete responders'; 'In 42 melanoma patients treated with CTLA-4 blockade using ipilimumab (Van Allen et al., 2015), it was lower in the two complete-responders'; Riaz: 'downregulated early on-treatment specifically in responders ... pre-treatment expression ... was not associated with response'. Signatures from Hugo 2016/Riaz 2017 were used only as alternative predictors/comparators (Table S6A). Other ICB cohorts not among 12: own validation cohort 1 (26 pts longitudinal), own validation cohort 2 (112 anti-PD-1; main claim), own scRNA cohort; mouse anti-CTLA-4 (Lesterhuis 2015). Hugo 2015 MAPKi cohort (non-ICB). URLs: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6410377/ ; https://github.com/livnatje/ImmuneResistance (Output/Tables/TableS4A_resistance.program.csv) | Caveats: bhklab 108-gene list: 91 symbols map to Table S4A, 88 of them in the Exclusion (up/down) components (17 symbols not found, likely aliases e.g. NIFK/MKI67IP, BUD23/WBSCR22, ADGRG1/GPR56); exact rule that produced this 108-gene subset not verified, but all program components derive from own scRNA + TCGA + CRISPR screen, none from the 12 cohorts. outcome_guided=no for the exclusion program; if the union 'resistance program' were meant, its post-treatment part used ICI-resistant vs untreated status in the authors' own scRNA cohort (outcome-related, not among 12). Main ICB claim established in own validation cohort 2.

development_data: KEYNOTE-012 (bladder, gastric, HNSCC, TNBC) + KEYNOTE-028 (anal, biliary, CRC, esophageal, ovarian) pembrolizumab, n=220, NanoString; elastic-net on ORR; validated in 96 HNSCC (KEYNOTE-012)
evidence: Ayers et al. JCI 2017 (PMC5531419; local txt 28650338.txt; Table 2 image https://www.jci.org/articles/view/91190/table/2). All data are Merck pembrolizumab trials on a NanoString 680-gene panel: Results 'a set of baseline biopsies from 19 patients with metastatic melanoma enrolled in the KEYNOTE-001 study ... was used as a pilot data set'; 'confirmed using expression data from an additional cohort of 62 patients with metastatic melanoma treated with pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-001'; refined signatures tested in KEYNOTE-012 HNSCC (n=40/43) and gastric (n=33); final GEP from 'KEYNOTE-012 (bladder, gastric, HNSCC, and TNBC) and KEYNOTE-028 (anal canal, biliary, colorectal, esophageal, and ovarian)' (n=220) and validated in 96 PD-L1-unselected HNSCC from KEYNOTE-012. No public cohort (Hugo, Van Allen or any of the 12) is mentioned anywhere in the text; Riaz/Gide/Kim/Mariathasan etc. were published after this paper (JCI online June 2017). Other ICB cohorts used (not among the 12): KEYNOTE-001 melanoma, KEYNOTE-012, KEYNOTE-028. Gene-set identity: bhklab Tcell-inflamed_Ayers (18 genes: CCL5, CD27, CD274, CD276, CD8A, CMKLR1, CXCL9, CXCR6, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DRB1, HLA-E, IDO1, LAG3, NKG7, PDCD1LG2, TIGIT, PSMB10, STAT1) = the final 18-gene T cell-inflamed GEP. Methods (Statistics): '220 patients ... from KEYNOTE-012 ... and KEYNOTE-028 ... were used in an elastic net penalized regression model for objective response to select a final set of genes and their weighting'; validated in 'a PD-L1-unselected cohort of 96 patients with HNSCC from KEYNOTE-012 who were not involved in prior testing or the training'. | Caveats: Paper's GEP uses regression-coefficient weights and housekeeping normalisation; bhklab file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/Tcell-inflamed_Ayers.csv has weight=1 for all genes (unweighted mean), so the tested score differs from the published weighted GEP. None of the 12 cohorts involved.

development_data: Exploratory biomarker analysis within POPLAR (phase 2 RCT, atezolizumab vs docetaxel, previously treated NSCLC; enrolled Aug 2013-Mar 2014): 8-gene T-effector/IFN-g-associated signature (CD8A, GZMA, GZMB, IFNG, EOMES, CXCL9, CXCL10, TBX21) based on T-effector biology; evaluated against OS in POPLAR.
evidence: Abstract (PubMed/Europe PMC): 'Biomarkers were assessed in an exploratory analysis... In our exploratory analysis, patients with pre-existing immunity, defined by high T-effector-interferon-g-associated gene expression, had improved overall survival with atezolizumab.' Only POPLAR patients (n=287 randomized) were analysed. Crossref reference list (31 refs) contains none of the 12 cohort papers; signature-related refs are biology/prior atezolizumab work (Herbst 2014 Nature phase I correlates, Powles 2014 Nature bladder, Rooney 2015 Cell cytolytic activity, perforin/granzyme, Eomes and T-bet papers). Dates: Lancet online 10 Mar 2016 (print Apr 2016) - predates Hugo (online 17 Mar 2016) and all other cohorts except Van Allen (Sep 2015), which is not cited. Other ICB cohort used (NOT among the 12): POPLAR (NCT01903993). Sources: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:26970723, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/S0140-6736(16)00587-0, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/Teff-IFNG_Fehrenbacher.csv (8 genes). | Caveats: COULD NOT READ FULL TEXT/APPENDIX: thelancet.com returned 403. Blank cells are certain (dates + abstract + reference list). Not verified from Methods: whether the 8 genes were fixed before POPLAR outcome analysis (reported as 'predefined/exploratory') and how the high/low cutoff was set (commonly reported as median) - hence outcome_guided 'unclear'. POPLAR is the C-type claim cohort but is not among the 12.

development_data: Predefined literature gene set (Teff: CD8A, EOMES, PRF1, IFNG, CD274; cited to POPLAR, Fehrenbacher 2016 ref 24); applied in IMmotion150 RCC (atezolizumab +/- bevacizumab vs sunitinib), median split
evidence: Methods 'Gene expression analyses': 'Gene signatures were defined as follows: ... Teff24: CD8A, EOMES, PRF1, IFNG, and CD274 ... These three gene expression signatures were defined based on previously published associations with their respective biology.' Score = mean expression; 'high ... at or above median'. Only cohort analysed: IMmotion150 (263 pretreatment tumours with RNA-seq) - not among the 12. Miao 2018 (ref 50) cited only in Discussion regarding PBRM1 ('Our data does not support this finding'); no Miao data analysed. No other ICB cohorts. URL: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6721896/ | Caveats: None of the 12 cohorts used. Teff genes taken from ref 24 (POPLAR NSCLC atezolizumab trial, not among 12); whether the POPLAR-era Teff gene choice involved outcome data was not checked (outside this paper). Median cutoff is data-internal, not outcome-tuned.

development_data: VHIO (Vall d'Hebron) non-ICB prescreening FFPE samples: RNA-seq of 153 samples, GO immune-response genes (2,323) hierarchically clustered; cluster 1 (808 adaptive-immune/IFNG genes) reduced to 12 genes (CXCL9/10/11, IFNG, PRF1, IL7R, GZMA, GZMB, PDCD1, CTLA4, CD274, FOXP3) representing the cluster mean and chosen as known IO markers/targets; cutoffs (+/-0.75) from hierarchical/PAM clustering of 909 VHIO NanoString samples, 'independent of clinical outcomes'.
evidence: Results 'Development of the VIGex signature': clustering of 2,323 GO:0006955 genes in 153 VHIO FFPE RNA-seq samples; 'Cluster 1 encompassed 808 genes'; 'The final 12-gene set encompassed genes involved in immune activation ... and T cell exhaustion ... markers with a role as IO response predictors or representing potential IO drug targets'; categories from hierarchical + PAM clustering of 909 samples: 'This TME categorization was independent of clinical outcomes'. Clinical validation: 'The predictive performance of VIGex was assessed in an independent cohort of 98 patients enrolled in early-phase IO trials at VHIO'. Then: 'To further confirm the predictive power of the VIGex signature, we tested its performance in a metanalysis of publicly available gene expression datasets from patients treated with IO... 13 available datasets ... 877 patients' ; Fig 3E legend: 'Fumet.1,34 Fumet.2,34 Hugo,14 Hwang,35 Jung,36 Riaz,37 Braun,38 Liu,39 Mariathasan,40 Miao.1,41 Snyder,42 Van_Allen43 and Nathanson44'. Refs: 14 Hugo Cell 2016; 36 Jung Nat Commun 2019 (DNA methylation loss...); 37 Riaz Cell 2017; 38 Braun Nat Med 2020; 39 Liu Nat Med 2019; 40 Mariathasan Nature 2018; 41 Miao Science 2018; 43 Van Allen Science 2015. STAR Methods: meta-analysis datasets from a systematic review (published Jan 2015-Sep 2020; combos with chemo/targeted and neoadjuvant excluded); raw fastq re-quantified for Fumet.1/2, Hugo, Hwang, Jung, Riaz; processed data for Braun, Liu, Mariathasan, Miao.1, Snyder, Van_Allen; VIGex scored by GSVA; code at codeocean capsule 6760186 / predictio.ca. Other ICB cohorts NOT among the 12: VHIO early-phase IO cohort (n=98), GSE159067 (HNSCC, Foy), GSE161537 (NSCLC, Foy), VHIO NSCLC and MSI-H CRC cohorts, Fumet.1/Fumet.2 (Fumet 2018 BJC Dijon NSCLC - related to but not Limagne1), Hwang 2020, Snyder 2017 urothelial, Nathanson 2017. Sources: full-text PDF from UAB repository https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2023/303227/MED_VIGex.pdf (saved dl/grpE/MED_VIGex.pdf; cell.com and sciencedirect returned 403), Europe PMC abstract, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhklab/SignatureSets/main/data-raw/IO/VIGex_Hernando-Calvo.csv (12 genes match). | Caveats: All 8 public cohorts were used only to confirm the frozen signature after the VHIO 98-patient clinical validation ('to further confirm'), so V. The INSPIRE/Princess Margaret samples were used only for inter-laboratory (analytical) validation of 30 VHIO samples, not outcome. Fumet.1/2 = Fumet et al. Br J Cancer 2018 (PMID 30318514) Dijon NSCLC data, earlier than Limagne1 (2022) - Limagne1 left blank but flag possible patient overlap with Dijon datasets. Gide, Kim, Puch, Limagne1 not used. Which Braun arm (nivolumab vs everolimus) and Liu/Riaz subsets were included is not stated in the main text (meta-analysis pipeline from Bareche et al./PredictIO).

development_data: Non-ICB data: TCGA NSCLC expression (230 cases per NCC press release) and an in-house cohort of 22 NSCLC (NCC Hospital East + Osaka University Hospital; flow cytometry, RNA-seq, WES), comparing WNT/beta-catenin pathway activation in TMB-high non-inflamed vs inflamed tumours; mouse models with stepwise TMB. No patient ICB response data reported.
evidence: Abstract (PubMed/Europe PMC): 'activation of the WNT/beta-catenin signaling pathway contributed to the development of a noninflamed TME in tumors with high TMB. NSCLCs that lacked immune cell infiltration into the TME despite high TMB preferentially up-regulated the WNT/beta-catenin pathway... In our animal models... Combined treatment with PD-1 blockade and WNT/beta-catenin signaling inhibitors induced better antitumor immunity'. development_data: Own retrospective multi-institution NSCLC ICI cohort (OmniSeq; 120 pts from 10 US/EU institutions; 110 RECIST-evaluable; targeted RNA-seq of a 394-gene immune panel). The 10 genes are the manufacturer-annotated 'proliferation' function; this function was selected among 41 functions by association of tertiles with disease control in a training set (n=76, all sites except Duke) and in training+test (n=110); tertile cut-offs from a separate 167-patient multi-tumour OmniSeq reference population.
evidence: Methods 'Patients and clinical data': 110 evaluable pts 'divided into a test set (n = 34) from one institution with the most patients (Duke) and a training set (n = 76) from all other institutions'. Methods 'Data analysis': pairwise proportion (chi-square) tests of DC rates across low/medium/high tertiles for each of 41 biological functions. Results 'Immune-related gene functions': 'Proliferation was chosen for further evaluation based upon the identification as a significant factor in the training set as well as the combination of the training and test set.' Results 'Proliferative status': tertiles 'as compared to a separate reference population of 167 patients with multiple tumor types'. Data availability: own data not public (patent). None of the 12 cohorts (or any public ICB dataset) is mentioned or used; TCGA only cited in Discussion. Other ICB cohorts used (not among 12): own 120-pt NSCLC cohort only.
